class EnvironmentTailTests(DiscoveryFixture):
    """Source proof controls, outside the semantic parent mutation population."""

    def guarded_parts(self, source, catalog):
        message = "environment-tail source premise requires revalidation"
        start = "        let mut env_deps = Vec::new();\n        for l in text.lines() {\n"
        stop = "        for raw in dependency_files(&text, &d, &scratch, &canonical_scratch)? {"
        self.assertEqual((source.count(start), source.count(stop)), (1, 1), message)
        a = source.index(start)
        self.assertTrue(source[:a].endswith(
            '        let text = fs::read_to_string(&d).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", d.display()))?;\n'
            '        let mut files = BTreeSet::new();\n'), message)
        loop = source[a:source.index(stop, a)]
        tail = "                continue;\n"
        self.assertIn(loop.count(tail), (0, 1), message)
        clean = loop.replace(tail, "", 1)
        self.assertEqual(hashlib.sha256(clean.encode()).hexdigest(),
                         "c21a74dd0ccb9d0ac902e8ecf1e304e72ca53a6476689a2081aae55ce3d9579a", message)
        ending = "            }\n        }\n"
        self.assertTrue(clean.endswith(ending), message)
        before = clean[:-len(ending)] + tail + ending
        self.assertEqual(hashlib.sha256(before.encode()).hexdigest(),
                         "80e6db30d3affc38de38e1a0d3a2f2ab1330cb3caba9f7612809b7735a1f159b", message)
        normal_start = "fn normalise_dependency_environment("
        self.assertEqual(source.count(normal_start), 1, message)
        a = source.index(normal_start)
        normalizer = source[a:source.index("\n}", a) + 2]
        self.assertEqual(hashlib.sha256(normalizer.encode()).hexdigest(),
                         "78d73126518285065bab8249c74e6b6ad0ad14374da048179306d01b4e3571f8", message)
        allowed_start = "pub(crate) const ENV_ALLOWED:"
        self.assertEqual(catalog.count(allowed_start), 1, message)
        a = catalog.index(allowed_start)
        allowed = catalog[a:catalog.index("];", a) + 2]
        self.assertEqual(hashlib.sha256(allowed.encode()).hexdigest(),
                         "f731822faf63efbb30631f7d28194973deb3e6aeed22b464e8f3bf1e37211500", message)
        return before, before.replace(tail, "                // continue;\n", 1), clean, normalizer, allowed

    def test_environment_tail_fallthrough_requires_the_complete_terminal_scope(self):
        source = (ROOT / "xtask/src/trust.rs").read_text()
        catalog = (ROOT / "xtask/src/catalog_build.rs").read_text()
        before, comment, clean, normalizer, allowed = self.guarded_parts(source, catalog)
        self.assertIn("rustc 1.95.0 (59807616e 2026-04-14)", self.bounded(["rustc", "--version"]))
        # A future body suffix, different loop target/type, or changed collector premise
        # must invalidate this local proof. Accept only its two proved production shapes.
        actual_loop = before if before in source else clean
        for proved_loop in [before, clean]:
            self.assertEqual(self.guarded_parts(source.replace(actual_loop, proved_loop, 1), catalog),
                             (before, comment, clean, normalizer, allowed))
        suffix_loop = actual_loop.replace("            }\n        }\n",
                                          "            }\n            observe();\n        }\n", 1)
        altered = [
            (source.replace(actual_loop, suffix_loop, 1), catalog),
            (source.replace(actual_loop, before.replace("continue;", "continue 'outer;", 1), 1), catalog),
            (source.replace("for l in text.lines()", "for l in other.lines()", 1), catalog),
            (source.replace('l.strip_prefix("# env-dep:")', 'l.strip_prefix("# ENV-dep:")', 1), catalog),
            (source.replace('dep.replace(&encode(scratch), "")', 'dep.replace(&encode(scratch), "x")', 1), catalog),
            (source.replace("fs::read_to_string(&d)", "read_other_type(&d)", 1), catalog),
            (source, catalog.replace('"CARGO_CRATE_NAME",', '"OUT_DIR",', 1)),
        ]
        for changed_source, changed_catalog in altered:
            self.assertNotEqual((changed_source, changed_catalog), (source, catalog))
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(AssertionError, "environment-tail source premise requires revalidation"):
                self.guarded_parts(changed_source, changed_catalog)

        unheld = ("trust-undeclared-input: `fixture` in `producer` depends on the environment variable "
                  "`UNHELD`, which the commit does not hold")
        empty = ("trust-undeclared-input: `fixture` in `producer` depends on the environment variable "
                 "``, which the commit does not hold")
        lookalike = ("trust-undeclared-input: `fixture` in `producer` depends on the environment variable "
                     "`CARGO_PKGX_NAME`, which the commit does not hold")
        # name, text, expected environment records, expected NEW refusals, prior refusals,
        # scratch prefix, canonical prefix. Expectations do not come from either variant.
        cases = [
            ("empty", "", [], [], []),
            ("non-records", "plain\n # env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=x\n# Env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=x\n", [], [], []),
            ("accepted", "# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=alpha\n", ["CARGO_PKG_NAME=alpha"], [], []),
            ("allowlist", "# env-dep:CARGO_CRATE_NAME=fixture\n", ["CARGO_CRATE_NAME=fixture"], [], []),
            ("foreign", "# env-dep:UNHELD=x\n", ["UNHELD=x"], [unheld], []),
            ("empty-record", "# env-dep:\n", [""], [empty], []),
            ("lookalike", "# env-dep:CARGO_PKGX_NAME=x\n", ["CARGO_PKGX_NAME=x"], [lookalike], []),
            ("positions", "# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=first\nplain\n# env-dep:UNHELD=x\n# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=last\n",
             ["CARGO_PKG_NAME=first", "UNHELD=x", "CARGO_PKG_NAME=last"], [unheld], []),
            ("duplicates", "# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=a\n# env-dep:UNHELD=x\n# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=a\n# env-dep:UNHELD=x",
             ["CARGO_PKG_NAME=a", "UNHELD=x", "CARGO_PKG_NAME=a", "UNHELD=x"], [unheld, unheld], []),
            ("prior", "# env-dep:UNHELD=x\n", ["UNHELD=x"], [unheld], ["prior refusal"]),
            ("crlf", "# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=a\r\nplain\r\n# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=b\r\n",
             ["CARGO_PKG_NAME=a", "CARGO_PKG_NAME=b"], [], []),
            ("unicode", "# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION=étude💡\n", ["CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION=étude💡"], [], []),
            ("equals", "# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION=a=b=c\n", ["CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION=a=b=c"], [], []),
            ("unset", "# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME\n", ["CARGO_PKG_NAME"], [], []),
            ("scratch", "# env-dep:CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=__SCRATCH__/crate\n", ["CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=/crate"], [], []),
            ("canonical", "# env-dep:CARGO_MANIFEST_PATH=__CANON__/Cargo.toml\n", ["CARGO_MANIFEST_PATH=/Cargo.toml"], [], []),
        ]
        literal = lambda value: json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)
        vector = lambda values: ("vec![" + ",".join(literal(value) + ".to_owned()" for value in values) + "]"
                                 if values else "Vec::<String>::new()")
        cases = [(*row, "__SCRATCH__", "__CANON__") for row in cases]
        cases.append(("encoded", "# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION=work\\\\dir\\nline/x\n",
                      ["CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION=/x"], [], [], "work\\dir\nline", "__CANON__"))

        trace = textwrap.dedent("""
            struct TraceText<'a> { input: &'a str, events: std::rc::Rc<std::cell::RefCell<Vec<&'static str>>> }
            struct TraceLines<'a> { lines: std::str::Lines<'a>, events: std::rc::Rc<std::cell::RefCell<Vec<&'static str>>> }
            struct TraceLine<'a> { text: &'a str, events: std::rc::Rc<std::cell::RefCell<Vec<&'static str>>> }
            impl TraceText<'_> {
                fn lines(&self) -> TraceLines<'_> {
                    self.events.borrow_mut().push("lines");
                    TraceLines { lines:self.input.lines(), events:self.events.clone() }
                }
            }
            impl<'a> Iterator for TraceLines<'a> {
                type Item=TraceLine<'a>;
                fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
                    self.events.borrow_mut().push("next");
                    self.lines.next().map(|text| TraceLine { text, events:self.events.clone() })
                }
            }
            impl std::ops::Deref for TraceLine<'_> { type Target=str; fn deref(&self) -> &str { self.text } }
            impl Drop for TraceLine<'_> { fn drop(&mut self) { self.events.borrow_mut().push("drop-line"); } }
            impl Drop for TraceLines<'_> { fn drop(&mut self) { self.events.borrow_mut().push("drop-iterator"); } }
        """)

        def collector(name, body, *, drops=False, suffix=False):
            header = ("#[inline(never)]\nfn " + name + "(input: &str, scratch: &str, canonical_scratch: &str, "
                      "who: &str, crate_name: &str, refused: &mut Vec<String>)")
            if drops:
                header += (" -> (Vec<String>, Vec<&'static str>) {\n"
                           "    let events=std::rc::Rc::new(std::cell::RefCell::new(Vec::new()));\n"
                           "    let text=TraceText { input, events:events.clone() };\n")
                finish = "    let snapshot=events.borrow().clone();\n    (env_deps, snapshot)\n"
            else:
                header += " -> " + ("(Vec<String>, Vec<String>)" if suffix else "Vec<String>") + " {\n    let text=input;\n"
                finish = "    (env_deps, suffix)\n" if suffix else "    env_deps\n"
            if suffix:
                ending = "            }\n        }\n"
                self.assertEqual(body.count(ending), 1)
                body = body.replace(ending, "            }\n            suffix.push(l.to_owned());\n        }\n", 1)
                header += "    let mut suffix=Vec::new();\n"
            return header + body + finish + "}\n"

        program = allowed + "\n" + normalizer + trace
        for name, body in [("before", before), ("comment", comment), ("clean", clean)]:
            program += collector(name, body)
        for name, body in [("drop_before", before), ("drop_clean", clean)]:
            program += collector(name, body, drops=True)
        for name, body in [("suffix_before", before), ("suffix_clean", clean)]:
            program += collector(name, body, suffix=True)
        checks = []
        for label, text, env, refusal, prior, scratch, canonical in cases:
            for name in ["before", "comment", "clean"]:
                checks.append("{ let mut refused=" + vector(prior) + "; let env=" + name + "("
                              + ",".join(map(literal, [text, scratch, canonical, "producer", "fixture"]))
                              + ", &mut refused); assert_eq!(env," + vector(env) + ',"env:' + label + ':' + name
                              + '"); assert_eq!(refused,' + vector(prior + refusal) + ',"refusal:' + label + ':' + name + '"); }')
        events = '["lines","next","drop-line","next","drop-line","next","drop-line","next","drop-iterator"]'
        for name in ["drop_before", "drop_clean"]:
            checks.append('{ let mut refused=Vec::new(); let (env,events)=' + name + '("# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=a\\nplain\\n# env-dep:UNHELD=x\\n",'
                          '"__SCRATCH__","__CANON__","producer","fixture",&mut refused); assert_eq!(env,' + vector(["CARGO_PKG_NAME=a", "UNHELD=x"])
                          + '); assert_eq!(refused,' + vector([unheld]) + '); assert_eq!(events,' + events + '); }')
        checks.append('let mut refused=Vec::new(); let left=suffix_before("# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=a\\nplain\\n","S","C","producer","fixture",&mut refused);'
                      'let right=suffix_clean("# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=a\\nplain\\n","S","C","producer","fixture",&mut refused);'
                      'assert_eq!(left.1,' + vector(["plain"]) + '); assert_eq!(right.1,' + vector(["# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=a", "plain"])
                      + '); assert_ne!(left.1,right.1);')
        checks.append('match std::env::args().nth(1).as_deref() { '
                      'Some("wrong-env") => { let mut r=Vec::new(); assert_eq!(clean("# env-dep:CARGO_PKG_NAME=a","S","C","producer","fixture",&mut r),'
                      + vector(["WRONG"]) + ',"wrong env literal"); }, '
                      'Some("wrong-refusal") => { let mut r=Vec::new(); clean("# env-dep:UNHELD=x","S","C","producer","fixture",&mut r); assert!(r.is_empty(),"wrong refusal literal"); }, '
                      'Some("wrong-suffix") => assert_eq!(left.1,right.1,"wrong suffix equality"), '
                      'Some("wrong-drop") => { let mut r=Vec::new(); let (_,e)=drop_clean("plain","S","C","producer","fixture",&mut r); assert_eq!(e,["drop-iterator","next"],"wrong drop order"); }, _ => {} }')
        program += 'fn main() {\n' + '\n'.join(checks) + '\nprintln!("environment-tail controls: 17 literals/3 forms, drops and distinguishing suffix held");\n}\n'
        path = self.base / "environment-tail.rs"
        path.write_text(program)

            self.assertIn("17 literals/3 forms, drops and distinguishing suffix held", self.bounded([str(binary)]))

                                      ("wrong-suffix", "wrong suffix equality"), ("wrong-drop", "wrong drop order")]:

### Proved environment-tail removal

The [proved redundant tail](#environment-loop-tail-control-proof) is now removed from `xtask/src/trust.rs`. The Rust change is exactly one line. Environment normalization, record/refusal ordering and subsequent dependency handling keep the same behavior for the complete source domain proved earlier. All semantic test bodies and both trust/observer reason files remain byte-identical. No generic continue reason is added.

Whole source SHA-256 changes from `9616b59ff2bc394e6471570bfaf857971671fda4a12c4fb745e557d2d21a1751` to `527f68d5787b16b5e7f9e31942772bcc548f735d017ef95a5e30180a5012a9b5`. Its production prefix is now `080a15a2d2509caf4ea79c557dced56942e20c2fb1599ee0e3e414b3fa66992e`. The normalizer and allowlist, every preceding/following statement and the complete Rust test section are preserved. The source proof establishes retirement; the absence of a mutation candidate does not establish equivalence.

#### Source-guard revalidation before refresh

The maintained terminal-scope control passes on cleaned production before any old hash is refreshed. Both complete-prefix guards then correctly refuse their old source bindings. After those two bindings are updated, the full50 operator suite catches a third binding in the [observer explicit-close proof](#observer-explicit-close-assessment): it hashes the caller prefix without the newline immediately before the test attribute. Its actual compiled close timing/protocol control passes, while its old source-premise guard refuses. The complete failed run and restored inputs are retained below.

The additional guard is qualified against the exact proved removal and unchanged observer/controller source and reason files. Its new newline-trimmed caller digest is `6a210d1810a3dbd5adecf861f77200a9846887f51f9dee8f6683ab16b8a88118`. Only three hash literals change in the Python controls. The same complete50-test suite then passes: actual pinned Cargo suffix controls, absolute-cwd and close-protocol controls, all prior operator cases and the new terminal-scope proof. The source/guard inverse reconstructs both prior files exactly; no old test assertion is weakened.

#### Complete current candidate reconciliation

Fresh loaded discovery and the actual native CLI list agree on1413 current production candidates, against1414 before cleanup. Exactly `L772.stmt.221` is retired. All other operator kinds, original text and physical span movements bind one to one. Some native replacement bytes intentionally change: the maintained generator derives fresh identifier prefixes from physical line numbers. A draft byte-equality assumption refused this difference; inspection of the native `loop_header` generator identified its complete cause.

There are303 such replacements:201 iterator and102 guard candidates. Each changes only a bijective prefix rename of `it/k/first/last`; its old/new fresh prefixes are absent from the corresponding complete source, preventing capture. Every other replacement byte is exact. Four altered mapping controls are refused, including an incorrect generated prefix. The complete mappings and native-list identity are durable below, without projecting any current native outcome from historical results.

All23 current reason sites persist. The historically killed non-tail continue `L1310.stmt.452` maps to `L1309.stmt.451`. The next separate checkpoint must execute that current candidate and every current reason against all current semantic parents, with strict justified outcomes and complete original/copied-input/name restoration. This leaf does not claim a fresh kill or E, and does not close the environment parent, full compiler scope, caller/global sweeps or independent review.

#### Final commit gate and retained evidence

The final focused tier is `make focused`. This commit is made only after that tier passes on the complete staged tree and its stamp names the same tree, with the pinned book build and doctrine gates also passing. The commit message records that staged-tree identity. All330 prior archives and the exact new permanent-control seal remain intact. Three task states reconstruct from the retained input commit; false identities and a truncated seal are rejected. Staging review corrected the new audit adapter’s intended-file list to include the separately byte-verified new seal; no older archive changed. The commit hook also refused a shortened log entry: its required work-unit/leaf prefix is now restored and checked before the final tier. Every previous book byte is retained.

Thus both predicates choose the same first pair or the same empty default; the unchanged fifteen-byte slice starts after the same complete ASCII prefix at a valid UTF-8 boundary and returns identical bytes, preserving dep-info selection and subsequent behavior. Permanent exact production/controller/observer/base/configuration/metadata/parser/tree/module/dependency/pin guards outside semantic tests, actual compiled original/edit, complete real ordinary/incremental/mixed argv and three consumed libraries, literal/constructor/adjacency controls, wider changed-output and short/Unicode panic witnesses, nineteen altered-premise controls and three wrong-oracle controls delimit the proof. Wider argv is explicitly not equivalent; finite producer agreement is not the proof. This conditional lemma covers actual successful invocations by that pinned producer; other judged-tree toolchain producers are outside it. Revalidate producer/pin, both callers, environment/config/admissions/preflight, transitive readers/module/dependency wiring, constructors/adjacency, record filter or extraction/slicing changes. </details>

#### Executable final checkpoint adapters

The adapters use repository-relative paths, runtime-derived roots and a repository-only write profile. Toolchain/OS inputs are necessary read-only host dependencies. The retained input commit plus captured deltas and immutable producer identities reconstruct the measurement inputs; the copied-tree index metadata is borrowed explicitly and does not claim a copied Git index. The plan’s planning-only label is retained as its exact pre-execution artifact; the native receipt supplies the actual verdict.

from pathlib import Path
import hashlib,json,re,subprocess,sys

out=Path('target/environment-tail-final-checkpoint')
base='a32d99d975fdbc741d154ffb2a80c61813e592d8'
B=chr(96)
def sha(data):return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
def prior(name):return subprocess.check_output(['git','show',base+':'+name])
def obj(kind,data):return hashlib.sha1(kind.encode()+b' '+str(len(data)).encode()+b'\0'+data).hexdigest()
def span(data,identity):
 a=data.index(('- ID: '+B+identity+B).encode())
 tail=data[a+1:]
 ends=[a+1+m.start() for m in re.finditer(rb'(?m)^- ID: |^## ',tail)]
 return a,min(ends) if ends else len(data)

execution=json.loads((out/'execution.json').read_text())
inputs=json.loads((out/'native-inputs.json').read_text())
assert subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','--show-object-format'],text=True).strip()=='sha1'
archive_name='docs/task-history/M3/M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.5.1.2.md'
index_name='docs/task-history/INDEX.md'
task_name='docs/tasks/M3.md'
identities=['M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.5.1.2','M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.5.2']
if '--capture' in sys.argv:
 changes=[];reconstructed=prior(task_name);current=Path(task_name).read_bytes()
 for identity in identities:
  a,b=span(reconstructed,identity);x,y=span(current,identity)
  replacement=current[x:y]
  changes.append(dict(file=task_name,identity=identity,before_sha256=sha(reconstructed[a:b]),replacement=replacement.decode()))
  reconstructed=reconstructed[:a]+replacement+reconstructed[b:]
 assert reconstructed==current
 old_index=prior(index_name);index=Path(index_name).read_bytes()
 row=next(line for line in index.splitlines(keepends=True) if line.startswith(('| '+B+identities[0]+B+' |').encode()))
 assert index.replace(row,b'',1)==old_index
 payload=dict(base_commit=base,task_replacements=changes,history_index_row=row.decode(),history_index_insertion_byte_offset=index.index(row),archive_file=archive_name,archive_source_file=task_name,archive_identities=identities[:1])
 (out/'input-reconstruction-delta.json').write_text(json.dumps(payload,indent=2)+'\n')

payload=json.loads((out/'input-reconstruction-delta.json').read_text())
assert payload['base_commit']==base and payload['archive_file']==archive_name
overrides={}
for change in payload['task_replacements']:
 old=overrides.get(change['file'],prior(change['file']));a,b=span(old,change['identity'])
 assert sha(old[a:b])==change['before_sha256']
 overrides[change['file']]=old[:a]+change['replacement'].encode()+old[b:]
old=prior(payload['archive_source_file']);blocks=[]
for identity in payload['archive_identities']:
 a,b=span(old,identity);assert old[a:b].endswith(b'\n')
 blocks.append(old[a:b-1])
archive=b'\n'.join(blocks)
if not archive.endswith(b'\n'):archive+=b'\n'
assert sha(archive)==inputs['regular'][archive_name]['sha256']
overrides[archive_name]=archive
old_index=prior(index_name);offset=payload['history_index_insertion_byte_offset']
assert isinstance(offset,int) and 0<=offset<=len(old_index)
overrides[index_name]=old_index[:offset]+payload['history_index_row'].encode()+old_index[offset:]
metadata={}
for raw in subprocess.check_output(['git','ls-tree','-r','-z',base]).split(b'\0'):
 if not raw:continue
 head,name=raw.split(b'\t',1);mode,kind,oid=head.decode().split(' ')
 metadata[name.decode()]=(mode,kind,oid)
assert set(inputs['regular'])=={name for name,(mode,kind,oid) in metadata.items() if kind=='blob'}|{archive_name}
assert set(inputs['gitlinks'])=={name for name,(mode,kind,oid) in metadata.items() if kind=='commit'}
for filename,entry in inputs['regular'].items():
 data=overrides[filename] if filename in overrides else prior(filename)
 assert sha(data)==entry['sha256'],filename
 assert obj('blob',data)==entry['index_oid'],filename
 assert entry['index_mode']==(metadata[filename][0] if filename in metadata else '100644'),filename
for filename,oid in inputs['gitlinks'].items():assert metadata[filename]==('160000','commit',oid)

def tree_hash(path,update):
 spec=base+(':'+path if path else '')
 rows={}
 for raw in subprocess.check_output(['git','ls-tree','-z',spec]).split(b'\0'):
  if not raw:continue
  head,name=raw.split(b'\t',1);mode,kind,oid=head.split(b' ')
  rows[name]=(mode.lstrip(b'0'),kind,oid.decode())
 for filename,oid in update.items():
  parent=filename.rsplit('/',1)[0] if '/' in filename else ''
  if parent==path:rows[filename.rsplit('/',1)[-1].encode()]=(b'100644',b'blob',oid)
 body=[]
 for name,(mode,kind,oid) in sorted(rows.items(),key=lambda item:item[0]+(b'/' if item[1][1]==b'tree' else b'')):
  relative=(path+'/' if path else '')+name.decode()
  if kind==b'tree' and any(filename.startswith(relative+'/') for filename in update):oid=tree_hash(relative,update)
  body.append(mode+b' '+name+b'\0'+bytes.fromhex(oid))
 return obj('tree',b''.join(body))

oids={name:obj('blob',data) for name,data in overrides.items()}
assert tree_hash('',{})==subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse',base+'^{tree}'],text=True).strip()
assert tree_hash('',oids)==execution['held_tree']
false=[]
for change in payload['task_replacements']:
 name=change['file'];current=overrides[name]
 a,b=span(current,change['identity']);x,y=span(prior(name),change['identity'])
 bad=dict(oids);bad[name]=obj('blob',current[:a]+prior(name)[x:y]+current[b:])
 assert tree_hash('',bad)!=execution['held_tree'];false.append('missing-task-delta:'+change['identity'])
for name,label in [(index_name,'missing-history-row'),(archive_name,'missing-new-seal')]:
 bad=dict(oids)
 if name==archive_name:bad.pop(name)
 else:bad[name]=obj('blob',prior(name))
 assert tree_hash('',bad)!=execution['held_tree'];false.append(label)
receipt=dict(status='reconstructed',scope='Read-only retained commit plus exact task/seal/index delta; no unreachable-tree dependency, Git writes or submodule implementation reads',base_commit=base,held_tree=execution['held_tree'],regular_inputs=len(inputs['regular']),opaque_gitlinks=len(inputs['gitlinks']),override_paths=sorted(overrides),negative_controls=false,delta_sha256=sha((out/'input-reconstruction-delta.json').read_bytes()))
(out/'input-reconstruction.json').write_text(json.dumps(receipt,indent=2)+'\n')
print('Held input reconstruction:',len(inputs['regular']),'regular blobs; exact root tree;',len(false),'false derivations refused')

### Disposable Git fixtures policy conflict

**The director approved the fixture exception on2026-10-20; owner `M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.3` verifies it next.** The session directive §21 forbids writes to every other Git repository. The mandated test harness creates, stages and commits separate disposable Git repositories under this project’s target directory. The routine pre-commit `README-ROUTES` check also initializes one, so the literal rule initially blocked the ordinary commit workflow. The question was raised before further fixture execution; the director’s explicit exception below now authorizes that workflow. No permissions setting change is needed.

The evidence is concrete: `xtask/src/trust.rs` contains the fixture constructor, later-commit helper and binding-layout initialization; their Git helper invokes real Git in the fixture directory. Read-only common-directory observations of the existing main and sweep-copy fixtures prove separate Git metadata. `scripts/check_readme_routes.sh` calls its scratch initialization from the normal scan; the current README bounds enable it, and the doctrine/hook chain reaches it. Six changed evidence inputs are rejected. These named sites are not a complete repository-wide fixture census.

The native run above had already finished when the conflict was recognized and did use the maintained fixture harness. Later diagnosis only reads source and existing Git metadata; it neither launches a new fixture nor claims that prior execution was fixture-free. A sandbox that confines writes to the repository volume does not itself prevent nested Git repository writes. The boundary’s canonical record is `docs/decisions/decision_repository-boundary-read-only.md`.

The pre-approval observations and original blocked finding below remain historical records. They do not supersede the director’s subsequent approval. Normal commit hooks run; no hook bypass is used. The new exception does not change any native outcome or close the four adequacy obligations.

### Disposable fixture exception

The director expressly allows disposable project-owned Git fixtures under this repository’s ignored `target/`. They may be initialized, populated, committed, recreated and removed for tests, hooks and diagnostics. Maintained external repositories and submodules remain read-only, including checkouts placed or linked under target. Same-volume storage and sealed-evaluation rules still apply. The canonical bootstrap `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions/decision_repository-boundary-read-only.md` state the exception.

Actual `git check-ignore -v` reports `.gitignore:2:/target` for both the trust fixture’s Git metadata and the normal hook’s fixture path; `git ls-files -- target` lists no tracked target files. Ignoring artifacts keeps them out of ordinary commits; the director’s explicit approval, rather than the ignore rule alone, authorizes the disposable repositories. The literal reply and command output are retained below. The separately committed .6.3 verification will exercise the approved fixture and real normal-hook path before survivor repairs.

## Disposable Git fixtures — director ruling pending

**Observed 2026-10-20; P0 owner `M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.3`.** The session directive §21
forbids writes in every other Git repository, while `README.md`/`COMMIT.md` mandate tests and
hooks whose maintained implementation initializes disposable repositories. This record does
not invent an exception or amend the rule. The director must settle its scope.

`xtask/src/trust.rs::tests::fixture` initializes, stages and commits a repository under
`target/trust-tests/`; `Fixture::commit` creates later commits, and `binding_layout` initializes
another repository. Read-only `rev-parse` observations confirm distinct Git common directories
for `target/trust-tests/clean/repo` and its native-sweep copy under
`target/mutation-sweep/tree/target/trust-tests/clean/repo`. These are generated project-owned
fixtures, not upstream project repairs. Their separate Git metadata is the scope question.

The normal `scripts/check_readme_routes.sh::hint_live_snapshots` path also runs `git init`
under `target/doctrine_scratch/readme_routes/live_snapshots_hint`; the README bounds row in
`LIVE_DOCUMENT_SIZE_CONTAINMENT.md` enables that branch. It is called by the ordinary
pre-commit doctrine registry, not only by a self-test. The source makes this dependency
reproducible without executing the disputed operation. Other inspected gate self-tests also
use fixtures; this is evidence of named sites, not a complete repository-wide census.

The initial dependency-path native run had already finished when this conflict was recognized:
four survivors, strict exit1, full201 semantic parents, all1153 regular original/copied inputs
restored. That execution did use the existing fixture harness; it is not described as a
fixture-free run. Subsequent observation is read-only. No further fixture execution or hook
bypass is authorized by this finding, and the repository-volume sandbox alone does not enforce
the nested-repository boundary. The prepared assessment cannot be called committed or clean
while the normal hook is blocked.

Required ruling: either permit disposable test/diagnostic repositories created under this
project's `target/`, with no writes to maintained external repositories or submodules; or keep
§21 literal and migrate affected tests/hooks before executing them. The owner implements and
verifies the selected route before resuming PNT. A permissions UI setting supplies no policy
exception. Full observation, contracts, assessment and portable receipts are retained in
`docs/book/src/annex-trust-proofs.md` under the disposable-fixtures and initial-assessment headings.

A dimension another\ndoctrine already owns is marked with that doctrine and not repeated here. Lowering a ceiling is free. The removed text remains exactly\n  retrievable: \u0060git show 2ae5559:LIVE_STATUS.md\u0060, sha256 \u00604910305c\u2026\u0060, 42 110 bytes, with the same for the other\n  two, recorded in the leaf. \u0060COMMIT.md\u0060 now says a snapshot changes only when the state it shows changes.\n<!-- LIVE-DOCUMENT-SIZE-CONTAINMENT-LOCAL-ADOPTION:END -->\n\n---\n\n# Live-Document Size-Containment Doctrine\n\nThis project-neutral, project-agnostic, and harness-neutral doctrine keeps\nlong-lived documentation useful as a bounded working set while preserving\ndurable information in addressable storage. It applies to human-authored\ndocuments, generated indexes, work records, manuals, ledgers, and historical\narchives. It does not prescribe a product domain, authoring tool, agent, build\nsystem, or repository layout.\n\n## Authority and adoption\n\nAfter adoption, the adopting project owns its copy. Cite the project's owner\nand adoption or revision date together with the project-owned doctrine file.\nNever cite a vendor-, agent-, or harness-specific bootstrap file as authority.\nBootstrap files may make the doctrine discoverable; they do not make it\nbinding.\n\nKeep project-specific authority, paths, thresholds, measurements, storage\nchoices, and migration decisions in a clearly fenced local adoption note or a\nseparate data registry. Keep them out of this neutral body. The copied doctrine\nis authoritative; its origin is a template rather than an upstream, so later\nchanges are adopted only through explicit local review.\n\n## Core invariant\n\nA bounded live view and a durable history are different products. The live\nview answers what a reader needs now; the durable store preserves what must\nremain recoverable. No surface may be both an indefinitely growing history and\na mandatory current read.\n\nEvery governed surface must declare:\n\n- its stable identifier, owner, audience, and canonical authority;\n- its lifecycle and storage topology;\n- independent reviewed health targets and inclusive enforcement ceilings for\n  lines, bytes, and maximum content-line bytes, plus file-count and aggregate\n  dimensions for collections unless a product-sized maintained-reference\n  contract replaces fixed aggregate caps with exact per-change authority;\n- warning and rollover-required milestones measured against health targets;\n- the operation that bounds it: overwrite, partition, regenerate, seal,\n  rotate, archive, supersede, or freeze;\n- how a reader finds current material and retrieves retained history; and\n- the mechanical check that rejects missing, stale, cyclic, or over-limit\n  declarations.\n\nRouting is transitive. A bounded file that sends overflow to an unbounded\nneighbor has not contained anything.\n\nReader navigation and author overflow are different route kinds. A reader may\nlegitimately navigate to immutable history. Author guidance may also identify\nexact history already captured by the durable version-history workflow, but it\nmust not redirect appendable prose into an immutable or frozen terminal.\nInventory both without forcing them to have the same destinations. Derive\nauthor candidates from enforcers' emitted failure guidance as well as\nhand-authored route data; an undeclared path-shaped hint is a real pressure\nedge and must fail closed.\n\nA collection front door must state what completeness means. A literal table of\ncontents proves every member, a generated index names its reproducible source,\nor an explicit query contract defines the complete target expansion. Presence\nof an index file alone proves none of these. Likewise, a human evidence map is\nonly trustworthy when every fenced repository-relative path resolves\nmechanically in the resulting tree.\n\n## Boundedness, currency, and truth\n\nBoundedness does not imply currency, and currency does not imply unrestricted\nsemantic truth. Size and route checks prove only their declared structural\nproperties. A current surface may opt into a named, lifecycle-specific\ncurrency contract backed by a calibrated local verifier. Only that declaration\nauthorizes the currency claim; the verifier must execute in the unconditional\ndoctrine path and its failure must fail closed.\n\nThe neutral doctrine never infers staleness from the newest date, the number of\ndistinct dates, file age, or a universal threshold. Closure facts legitimately\nput old dates in current roadmaps, while archive and frozen dates are expected\nto remain old. Historical terminals and frozen records are therefore exempt\nfrom current-state contracts. A local verifier may detect a document's exact\nself-contradiction or compare a projection with its canonical source, but its\ngrammar and false-positive calibration belong to the adopting project.\n\n## Derived-state containment\n\nMechanically owned current state is a separate truth boundary. If a canonical\nsystem can answer a field's question exactly, deterministically, and cheaply,\nthe field is derived state rather than independent information. Classify each\nsuch maintained current-state field in one of two ways:\n\n1. **Derive on read.** Do not store the value. Keep the exact command or\n   accessor at the reader's point of need so the answer is computed from its\n   authority when requested. A value invalidated by the commit or write that\n   records it must always use this class; periodic correction cannot make a\n   self-invalidating copy coherent.\n2. **Verified copy.** Retain a value only because the copy itself is a\n   deliberate contract, published baseline, or bounded projection. Name its\n   canonical authority and recomputation method, and execute a verifier that\n   fails whenever the stored copy disagrees. Declaring a verifier without\n   running it is not verification.\n\nJudgement, intent, rationale, ownership, blockers, and a deliberately selected\nnext action are not mechanically derivable and remain ordinary authored\ncontent. An immutable evidence snapshot is also distinct from a mutable claim\nabout now: it must name an exact capture boundary such as a revision, digest,\ninvocation, or externally owned observation and remain under the applicable\nevidence, retention, archive, or frozen-identity contract. Removing the\nboundary or relabeling the snapshot as current turns it back into an\nunverified copy.\n\nField discovery is declared, not guessed. The adopting project keeps an\nexplicit bounded list of governed paths and exact field markers; the neutral\nchecker contains no project-specific names and does not infer semantics from\ndates, number shapes, or prose. Generated projections with declared canonical\ninputs and executed freshness already satisfy the verified-copy rule at\nsurface scope.\n\nBefore demoting a duplicate, compare it with its authority and inspect the\nauthority for divergence the convenient copy may have concealed. Preserve the\nreader's question in place through the derivation, repair the canonical source\nfirst if it is wrong, and only then remove the duplicate. A smaller document\nthat silently loses the answer or preserves a defective authority is not a\nsuccessful containment migration.\n\n## Lifecycle classes\n\n| Class | Purpose | Required containment |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| \u0060bounded_snapshot\u0060 | Current state, resume pointer, or concise landing/index view | Overwrite semantics, no embedded chronology, line/byte limits, and a stale-state check where derivable |\n| \u0060partitioned_canonical\u0060 | Finite or contract-bounded canonical material whose full content remains directly browsable | Stable semantic partitions, bounded table of contents, per-part/file-count/aggregate limits, and link/reconstruction checks |\n| \u0060maintained_reference\u0060 | Unique maintained product/specification prose whose aggregate follows legitimate product scope | Auditable audience/role/rationale, stable semantic parts, bounded complete mandatory index and navigation depth, per-part limits, and exact fresh authority for every aggregate change |\n| \u0060generated_projection\u0060 | Search map, catalog, or index derived from smaller canonical units | Reproducible generation, freshness proof, bounded root view and shards, and no unique facts in generated output |\n| \u0060rolling_ledger\u0060 | Ordered recent entries with historical value | Bounded current window, deterministic seal/rotation boundary, immutable segments, bounded index, and an archive transition before aggregate growth becomes unbounded |\n| \u0060archive_terminal\u0060 | Exact historical evidence not needed in ordinary reading | Immutable locator, identity and size proof, tool-neutral retrieval procedure, retention owner, and exclusion from mandatory bootstrap reads |\n| \u0060external_terminal\u0060 | History retained by an independently managed system | Named authority, retention commitment, stable query/export contract, and a failure policy if that contract disappears |\n| \u0060frozen_legacy\u0060 | Existing record awaiting an owned lifecycle decision | Exact content identity or equivalent write prohibition; it cannot accept new content or act as an overflow destination |\n\nA local adoption may define additional classes, but each must make growth stop,\nbecome predictably partitioned under fixed bounds, or govern product-scope\nchange through exact fresh authority. Renaming an append-only blob is not a new\nlifecycle.\n\n## Choose the storage topology from the information role\n\nDo not shard mechanically by arbitrary line count. Classify the information\nfirst:\n\n1. Current state belongs in an overwritten bounded snapshot.\n2. Unique maintained material that people browse belongs in semantic,\n   navigable partitions. If its aggregate follows legitimate product scope,\n   classify it as maintained reference and bound the read path plus each part\n   while authorizing every aggregate change exactly.\n3. A projection that can be recreated belongs in generated bounded shards; its\n   smaller canonical inputs remain authoritative.\n4. Exact chronology or evidence that is rarely read belongs in a query-first\n   archive after its current window closes.\n5. Content already present in a richer canonical source is proved duplicate,\n   then removed with a link rather than copied into another store.\n\nSharding controls per-read and per-file pressure, but it does not by itself\ncontrol aggregate storage. An ordinary partitioned collection keeps aggregate\nlimits. A maintained product reference instead measures aggregate files/lines/\nbytes and requires an exact, newly owned change record whenever they move;\nfixed aggregate targets are explicitly inapplicable rather than silently\nunlimited. A rolling ledger must still declare when sealed segments leave the\nlive collection for an archive terminal. The chosen topology must therefore\nbound the reader's working set and either bound or exactly govern the\ncollection's long-term aggregate change according to information role.\n\n## Derive pressure limits from the retained surface\n\nMeasure the deliberately reviewed live survivor and set independent line,\nbyte, and maximum content-line-byte health targets. For collections, also set\nper-part, file-count, and aggregate targets. Maximum line width is a separate\npressure axis: a generated table or dense record can remain pathological while\nthe file still passes total-line and total-byte limits. Measure raw content\nbytes deterministically, excluding LF and an optional preceding CR. Do not copy\nillustrative numbers from another adoption, and do not treat a current legacy\nsize as healthy merely because it was measured.\n\nThe exception is unique maintained product/specification prose. A fixed\naggregate target there is dishonest because legitimate scope changes with the\nproduct. Require fixed per-part limits, a complete mandatory index with its own\nline/byte bounds, bounded direct navigation, and exact aggregate baseline plus\nsigned per-change delta. A revision-aware adapter must reject stale, inexact,\nreused, or banked authority. Classification alone never waives a monolith's\nexisting debt; semantic partition and complete navigation land first.\n\nFor every measured dimension, declare two different values:\n\n- the **health target** describes the reviewed steady-state working set and is\n  the denominator for warning and rollover pressure; and\n- the **inclusive enforcement ceiling** rejects only \u0060actual > ceiling\u0060. It is\n  a quarantine boundary, not evidence that content below it is healthy.\n\nEach local registry selects two ordered milestones against the health target:\n\n- **warning**: investigation and an owned remediation become mandatory;\n- **rollover required**: ordinary appends stop unless the same change performs\n  the declared rollover.\n\nThe warning must leave enough capacity for the largest normal update plus the\nrollover transaction. A ceiling increase requires a new, separate, reviewed\nauthority record proving that the surface's user contract expanded; editing\nthe surface declaration alone cannot authorize itself. Lowering is free.\n\nAt first adoption, a surface already beyond warning or rollover may be entered\nas explicit transition debt only with its exact measured baseline, named\nremediation owner, deadline or ordered frontier, and unchanged ceiling.\nOnly records required to complete the containment transition may extend a\nrollover-debt surface; ordinary unrelated growth remains prohibited. The debt\nexception ends when the migration lands and can never excuse ceiling overflow.\nIts baseline cannot increase across revisions, but an atomic content reduction\nmay lower it so the ceiling can ratchet down. The current baseline plus owned\nallowance must fit below the ceiling. A\ndeclared ratchet band must also reject a ceiling that remains materially above\nboth actual use and the health target after pressure falls.\n\n## Atomic partition, rollover, and archive protocol\n\nA transition is complete only when one change performs and verifies all\napplicable steps:\n\n1. Stop writes to the source at a stable semantic, record, or time boundary.\n2. Classify retained information as canonical, derived, duplicate, or archival.\n3. Write the new partition, sealed segment, or archive record without altering\n   record order or identity.\n4. Record source and destination line counts, byte counts, and content digests;\n   when exact reconstruction is promised, prove it byte for byte.\n   Report complete-source identity, semantic closure, the live working-set\n   dimensions, and any truly unretained residue as four independent products.\n   Declare whether products overlap; never force disjoint arithmetic onto\n   retained source, semantic extracts, and live navigation views.\n5. Update the bounded current view, manifest, table of contents, predecessor/\n   successor links, and query route.\n6. Run link, freshness, ordering, uniqueness, retrieval, and pressure checks;\n   a declared executable must actually run successfully, not merely exist.\n7. Compare each duplicate with its authority, repair any divergence the copy\n   concealed, and only after those checks pass remove a live duplicate whose\n   derivation, retained copy, or archive retrieval has been proved.\n8. Commit the transition atomically so no durable state exposes half a move.\n\nFor a task-tree ledger, bound live narrative fields independently from the\nfile and collection ceilings. When repeated optional verification/checklist\nhistory becomes the scaling term, retain the complete live node graph, stop at\none exact predecessor, and replace only the historical suffix with a finite\nmanifest pointer. The verifier must retrieve and authenticate both the complete\npredecessor and the exact removed suffix, require a unique live pointer, count\nembedded markup as source bytes, and reject string-encoded numeric evidence.\nStructural child indexes remain governed by graph closure rather than the\nnarrative-field cap.\n\nSealed units are immutable. Corrections create a superseding record or segment\nrather than silently editing archived evidence.\n\n## Archive descriptor contract\n\nWhen bytes leave the live collection, a small tracked descriptor must preserve\nat least:\n\n- schema version and stable surface identifier;\n- former logical path and covered record, topic, or time range;\n- immutable revision or object locator;\n- line count, byte count, and content digest before removal;\n- a repository-root-relative or otherwise portable retrieval procedure;\n- the current-view, manifest, and replacement pointers;\n- the sealing reason, date, and verifier identity; and\n- an executable proof that retrieval reproduces the declared content.\n\nA version object is a conditional retention mechanism, not a self-proving\narchive. Every version-object use must name a bounded retention contract with\nan owner, an explicit reachability/backup guarantee, and an actionable\nrecovery procedure for shallow history or rewritten objects. If evidence must\nremain recoverable without that condition, prefer a content-addressed file on\nthe repository volume.\n\nRetrieval must not depend on a particular AI agent, editor, or harness. An\narchive descriptor is a controlled terminal, not permission to route new live\ncontent into an opaque dump.\n\n## Registry and mechanical enforcement\n\nKeep local declarations in data-only registries consumed by one deterministic\nchecker. Each registry must itself be finite: begin with schema-versioned\nmetadata declaring positive maximum data-record count, total file bytes, and\nraw JSON bytes per record; impose portable fail-safe ceilings as well as the\nadopter's tighter limits. Arrays need finite cardinalities, scalar fields need\nbyte limits, identifiers need closed domains, and unknown fields fail closed.\nThe registries are the local authority for class, paths, limits, milestones,\ngeneration or retrieval checks, and dependency routes. The checker must run\non the resulting tree for every commit and continuous-integration build,\nindependent of which paths changed.\n\nAt minimum, fail on:\n\n- an undeclared live surface or routing destination;\n- missing, malformed, oversized, or over-populated control-plane registry\n  metadata, record, scalar, or array;\n- an absolute, escaping, or otherwise forbidden persisted path;\n- a missing owner, lifecycle, limit, or retrieval/freshness control;\n- a route cycle or a route ending at an uncontrolled neighbor;\n- a stale generated projection or broken current/history link;\n- a declared derive-on-read field marker that remains stored, a missing reader\n  derivation, an off-surface field contract, or a verified copy whose authority\n  verifier is absent, unexecuted, degraded, or failing;\n- a mutable sealed/frozen unit or failed archive digest/retrieval proof;\n- a version object without a named retention owner, guarantee, and recovery\n  action, or migration evidence that conflates overlapping products;\n- warning without an owned remediation, rollover-required without the atomic\n  transition, actual usage above an inclusive ceiling, or stale debt headroom;\n- an unauthorized ceiling increase or rewritten debt baseline; and\n- an unclassified maintained reference, oversized part or mandatory index,\n  incomplete direct navigation, aggregate mismatch, or stale/reused/banked\n  aggregate-change authority.\n\nGenerated caches may accelerate the checker or search, but they are disposable\nand never the canonical copy.\n\n## Adoption checklist\n\n1. Add a project-owned copy and fence all local metadata away from this body.\n2. Inventory every live document, generated view, collection, route, and\n   historical terminal; follow routes transitively.\n3. Classify each surface by lifecycle and identify its actual canonical source.\n4. Classify mechanically owned current-state fields as derive-on-read or\n   verified copies; publish exact local markers, authorities, derivations, and\n   verifier contracts without heuristic field discovery.\n5. Measure lines, bytes, maximum content-line bytes, file counts, aggregates,\n   structure, and read path.\n6. Derive health targets from reviewed survivors and set separate inclusive\n   ceilings with only transaction-sized headroom.\n7. Open an owner for every surface already at warning or structurally\n   monolithic even if it remains below a numeric threshold.\n8. Choose bounded snapshot, semantic partitions, maintained reference,\n   generated shards, rolling ledger, archive, external, or frozen topology\n   from the information role.\n9. Prove any duplicate and compare its authority before deletion; prove any\n   archive before removing its live copy.\n10. Add the data registry, unconditional checker, positive/fail-closed tests,\n   and commit/CI wiring.\n11. Re-audit after each migration and periodically thereafter; lower limits to\n    the retained steady-state surface instead of preserving legacy headroom.\n"

The use of a stable sort\n        // is also important here because it ensures that paths of the same type retain the same relative\n        // ordering (for an unstable sort to work here, the list would need to retain the idx of each element\n        // and then sort by that idx when the type is equivalent.\n        library_paths.sort_by_key(|p| match p {\n            LibraryPath::CargoArtifact(_) => 0,\n            LibraryPath::External(_) => 1,\n        });\n\n        for path in library_paths.iter() {\n            rustc.arg(\"-L\").arg(path.as_ref());\n        }\n\n        for key in build_scripts.to_link.iter() {\n            let output = build_script_outputs.get(key.1).ok_or_else(|| {\n                internal(format!(\n                    \"couldn't find build script output for {}/{}\",\n                    key.0, key.1\n                ))\n            })?;\n\n            if key.0 == current_id {\n                if pass_l_flag {\n                    for name in output.library_links.iter() {\n                        rustc.arg(\"-l\").arg(name);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            for (lt, arg) in &output.linker_args {\n                // There was an unintentional change where cdylibs were\n                // allowed to be passed via transitive dependencies. For\n                // now, continue allowing it for cdylib only.\n                // See https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/9562\n                if lt.applies_to(target, mode)\n                    && (key.0 == current_id || *lt == LinkArgTarget::Cdylib)\n                {\n                    rustc.arg(\"-C\").arg(format!(\"link-arg={}\", arg));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nfn verbose_if_simple_exit_code(err: Error) -> Error {\n    // If a signal on unix (\u0060code == None\u0060) or an abnormal termination\n    // on Windows (codes like \u00600xC0000409\u0060), don't hide the error details.\n    match err\n        .downcast_ref::<ProcessError>()\n        .as_ref()\n        .and_then(|perr| perr.code)\n    {\n        Some(n) if cargo_util::is_simple_exit_code(n) => VerboseError::new(err).into(),\n        _ => err,\n    }\n}\n\nfn prebuild_lock_exclusive(lock: LockKey) -> Work {\n    Work::new(move |state| {\n        state.lock_exclusive(&lock)?;\n        Ok(())\n    })\n}\n\nfn downgrade_lock_to_shared(lock: LockKey) -> Work {\n    Work::new(move |state| {\n        state.downgrade_to_shared(&lock)?;\n        Ok(())\n    })\n}\n\n/// Link the compiled target (often of form \u0060foo-{metadata_hash}\u0060) to the\n/// final target. This must happen during both \"Fresh\" and \"Compile\".\nfn link_targets(\n    build_runner: &mut BuildRunner<'_, '_>,\n    unit: &Unit,\n    fresh: bool,\n) -> CargoResult<Work> {\n    let bcx = build_runner.bcx;\n    let outputs = build_runner.outputs(unit)?;\n    let export_dir = build_runner.files().export_dir();\n    let package_id = unit.pkg.package_id();\n    let manifest_path = PathBuf::from(unit.pkg.manifest_path());\n    let profile = unit.profile.clone();\n    let unit_mode = unit.mode;\n    let features = unit.features.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n    let json_messages = bcx.build_config.emit_json();\n    let executable = build_runner.get_executable(unit)?;\n    let mut target = Target::clone(&unit.target);\n    if let TargetSourcePath::Metabuild = target.src_path() {\n        // Give it something to serialize.\n        let path = unit\n            .pkg\n            .manifest()\n            .metabuild_path(build_runner.bcx.ws.build_dir());\n        target.set_src_path(TargetSourcePath::Path(path));\n    }\n\n    Ok(Work::new(move |state| {\n        // If we're a \"root crate\", e.g., the target of this compilation, then we\n        // hard link our outputs out of the \u0060deps\u0060 directory into the directory\n        // above. outputs.iter() {\n            let src = &output.path;\n            // This may have been a \u0060cargo rustc\u0060 command which changes the\n            // output, so the source may not actually exist.\n            if !src.exists() {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let Some(dst) = output.hardlink.as_ref() else {\n                destinations.push(src.clone());\n                continue;\n            };\n            destinations.push(dst.clone());\n            paths::link_or_copy(src, dst)?;\n            if let Some(ref path) = output.export_path {\n                let export_dir = export_dir.as_ref().unwrap();\n                paths::create_dir_all(export_dir)?;\n\n                paths::link_or_copy(src, path)?;\n            }\n        }\n\n        if json_messages {\n            let debuginfo = match profile.debuginfo.into_inner() {\n                TomlDebugInfo::None => machine_message::ArtifactDebuginfo::Int(0),\n                TomlDebugInfo::Limited => machine_message::ArtifactDebuginfo::Int(1),\n                TomlDebugInfo::Full => machine_message::ArtifactDebuginfo::Int(2),\n                TomlDebugInfo::LineDirectivesOnly => {\n                    machine_message::ArtifactDebuginfo::Named(\"line-directives-only\")\n                }\n                TomlDebugInfo::LineTablesOnly => {\n                    machine_message::ArtifactDebuginfo::Named(\"line-tables-only\")\n                }\n            };\n            let art_profile = machine_message::ArtifactProfile {\n                opt_level: profile.opt_level.as_str(),\n                debuginfo: Some(debuginfo),\n                debug_assertions: profile.debug_assertions,\n                overflow_checks: profile.overflow_checks,\n                test: unit_mode.is_any_test(),\n            };\n\n            let msg = machine_message::Artifact {\n                package_id: package_id.to_spec(),\n                manifest_path,\n                target: &target,\n                profile: art_profile,\n                features,\n                filenames: destinations,\n                executable,\n                fresh,\n            }\n            .to_json_string();\n            state.stdout(msg)?;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }))\n}\n\n// For all plugin dependencies, add their -L paths (now calculated and present\n// in \u0060build_script_outputs\u0060) to the dynamic library load path for the command\n// to execute.\nfn add_plugin_deps(\n    rustc: &mut ProcessBuilder,\n filter_dynamic_search_path(\n            output.library_paths.iter().map(AsRef::as_ref),\n            root_output,\n        ));\n    }\n    let search_path = paths::join_paths(&search_path, var)?;\n        let dir = get_dynamic_search_path(dir);\n        if dir.starts_with(&root_output) {\n            search_path.push(dir.to_path_buf());\n        } else {\n            debug!(\n                \"Not including path {} in runtime library search path because it is \\\n                 outside target root {}\",\n                dir.display(),\n                root_output.display()\n builds a static view of the invocation. Flags depending on the\n/// completion of other units will be added later in runtime, such as flags\n/// from build scripts.\nfn prepare_rustc(build_runner: &BuildRunner<'_, '_>, unit: &Unit) -> unit.pkg.manifest_path().display()\n            );\n        }\n        base.arg(\"-Z\").arg(\"crate-attr=feature(frontmatter)\");\n add_error_format_and_color(build_runner: &BuildRunner<'_, '_>, cmd: &mut ProcessBuilder) {\n    let enable_timings =\n        build_runner.bcx.gctx.cli_unstable().section_timings && build_runner.bcx.logger.is_some();\n    if enable_timings {\n        cmd.arg(\"-Zunstable-options\");\n    }\n\n    cmd.arg(\"--error-format=json\");\n    let mut json = String::from(\"--json=diagnostic-rendered-ansi,artifacts,future-incompat\");\n\n    if let MessageFormat::Short | MessageFormat::Json { short: true, .. } =\n        build_runner.bcx.build_config.message_format\n    {\n        json.push_str(\",diagnostic-short\");\n    } else if build_runner.bcx.gctx.shell().err_unicode()\n        && build_runner.bcx.gctx.cli_unstable().rustc_unicode\n    {\n        json.push_str(\",diagnostic-unicode\");\n    }\n\n    if enable_timings {\n        json.push_str(\",timings\");\n    }\n\n    cmd.arg(json);\n\n    let gctx = build_runner.bcx.gctx;\n    if let Some(width) = gctx.shell().err_width().diagnostic_terminal_width() {\n        cmd.arg(format!(\"--diagnostic-width={width}\"));\n    }\n}\n\n/// Adds essential rustc flags and environment variables to the command to execute.\nfn build_base_args(\n    build_runner: &BuildRunner<'_, '_>,\n    cmd: &mut ProcessBuilder,\n    unit: &Unit,\n) -> CargoResult<()> {\n    assert!(!unit.mode.is_run_custom_build());\n\n    let bcx = build_runner.bcx;\n    let Profile {\n        ref opt_level,\n        codegen_backend,\n        codegen_units,\n        debuginfo,\n        debug_assertions,\n        split_debuginfo,\n        overflow_checks,\n        rpath,\n        ref panic,\n        incremental,\n        strip,\n        rustflags: profile_rustflags,\n        trim_paths,\n        hint_mostly_unused: profile_hint_mostly_unused,\n        ..\n    } = unit.profile.clone();\n    let hints = unit.pkg.hints().cloned().unwrap_or_default();\n    let test = unit.mode.is_any_test();\n\n    let warn = |msg: &str| {\n        bcx.gctx.shell().warn(format!(\n            \"{}@{}: {msg}\",\n            unit.pkg.package_id().name(),\n            unit.pkg.package_id().version()\n        ))\n    };\n    let unit_capped_warn = |msg: &str| {\n        if unit.show_warnings(bcx.gctx) {\n            warn(msg)\n        } else {\n            Ok(())\n        }\n    };\n\n    cmd.arg(\"--crate-name\").arg(&unit.target.crate_name());\n\n    let edition = unit.target.edition();\n    edition.cmd_edition_arg(cmd);\n\n    add_path_args(bcx.ws, unit, cmd);\n    add_error_format_and_color(build_runner, cmd);\n    add_allow_features(build_runner, cmd);\n\n    let mut contains_dy_lib = false;\n    if !test {\n        for crate_type in &unit.target.rustc_crate_types() {\n            cmd.arg(\"--crate-type\").arg(crate_type.as_str());\n            contains_dy_lib |= crate_type == &CrateType::Dylib;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if unit.mode.is_check() {\n        cmd.arg(\"--emit=dep-info,metadata\");\n    } else if build_runner.bcx.gctx.cli_unstable().no_embed_metadata {\n        // Nightly rustc supports the -Zembed-metadata=no flag, which tells it to avoid including\n        // full metadata in rlib/dylib artifacts, to save space on disk. In this case, metadata\n        // will only be stored in .rmeta files.\n        // When we use this flag, we should also pass --emit=metadata to all artifacts that\n        // contain useful metadata (rlib/dylib/proc macros), so that a .rmeta file is actually\n        // generated. If we didn't do this, the full metadata would not get written anywhere.\n        // However, we do not want to pass --emit=metadata to artifacts that never produce useful\n        // metadata, such as binaries, because that would just unnecessarily create empty .rmeta\n        // files on disk.\n        if unit.benefits_from_no_embed_metadata() {\n            cmd.arg(\"--emit=dep-info,metadata,link\");\n            cmd.args(&[\"-Z\", \"embed-metadata=no\"]);\n        } else {\n            cmd.arg(\"--emit=dep-info,link\");\n        }\n    } else {\n        // If we don't use -Zembed-metadata=no, we emit .rmeta files only for rlib outputs.\n        // This metadata may be used in this session for a pipelined compilation, or it may\n        // be used in a future Cargo session as part of a pipelined compile.\n        if !unit.requires_upstream_objects() {\n            cmd.arg(\"--emit=dep-info,metadata,link\");\n        } else {\n            cmd.arg(\"--emit=dep-info,link\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    let prefer_dynamic = (unit.target.for_host() && !unit.target.is_custom_build())\n        || (contains_dy_lib && !build_runner.is_primary_package(unit));\n    if prefer_dynamic {\n        cmd.arg(\"-C\").arg(\"prefer-dynamic\");\n    }\n\n    if opt_level.as_str() != \"0\" {\n        cmd.arg(\"-C\").arg(&format!(\"opt-level={}\", opt_level));\n    }\n\n    if *panic != PanicStrategy::Unwind {\n        cmd.arg(\"-C\").arg(format!(\"panic={}\", panic));\n    }\n    if *panic == PanicStrategy::ImmediateAbort {\n        cmd.arg(\"-Z\").arg(\"unstable-options\");\n    }\n\n    cmd.args(&lto_args(build_runner, unit));\n\n    if let Some(backend) = codegen_backend {\n        cmd.arg(\"-Z\").arg(&format!(\"codegen-backend={}\", backend));\n    }\n\n    if let Some(n) = codegen_units {\n        cmd.arg(\"-C\").arg(&format!(\"codegen-units={}\", n));\n    }\n\n    let debuginfo = debuginfo.into_inner();\n    // Shorten the number of arguments if possible.\n    if debuginfo != TomlDebugInfo::None {\n        cmd.arg(\"-C\").arg(format!(\"debuginfo={debuginfo}\"));\n        // This is generally just an optimization on build time so if we don't\n        // pass it then it's ok. The values for the flag (off, packed, unpacked)\n        // may be supported or not depending on the platform, so availability is\n        // checked per-value. For example, at the time of writing this code, on\n        // Windows the only stable valid value for split-debuginfo is \"packed\",\n        // while on Linux \"unpacked\" is also stable.\n        if let Some(split) = split_debuginfo {\n            if build_runner\n                .bcx\n                .target_data\n                .info(unit.kind)\n                .supports_debuginfo_split(split)\n            {\n                cmd.arg(\"-C\").arg(format!(\"split-debuginfo={split}\"));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if let Some(trim_paths) = trim_paths {\n        trim_paths_args(cmd, build_runner, unit, &trim_paths)?;\n    }\n\n    cmd.args(unit.pkg.manifest().lint_rustflags());\n    cmd.args(&profile_rustflags);\n\n    // \u0060-C overflow-checks\u0060 is implied by the setting of \u0060-C debug-assertions\u0060,\n    // so we only need to provide \u0060-C overflow-checks\u0060 if it differs from\n    // the value of \u0060-C debug-assertions\u0060 we would provide.\n    if opt_level.as_str() != \"0\" {\n        if debug_assertions {\n            cmd.args(&[\"-C\", \"debug-assertions=on\"]);\n            if !overflow_checks {\n                cmd.args(&[\"-C\", \"overflow-checks=off\"]);\n            }\n        } else if overflow_checks {\n            cmd.args(&[\"-C\", \"overflow-checks=on\"]);\n        }\n    } else if !debug_assertions {\n        cmd.args(&[\"-C\", \"debug-assertions=off\"]);\n        if overflow_checks {\n            cmd.args(&[\"-C\", \"overflow-checks=on\"]);\n        }\n    } else if !overflow_checks {\n        cmd.args(&[\"-C\", \"overflow-checks=off\"]);\n    }\n\n    if test && unit.target.harness() {\n        cmd.arg(\"--test\");\n\n        // Cargo has historically never compiled \u0060--test\u0060 binaries with\n        // \u0060panic=abort\u0060 because the \u0060test\u0060 crate itself didn't support it.\n        // Support is now upstream, however, but requires an unstable flag to be\n        // passed when compiling the test. We require, in Cargo, an unstable\n        // flag to pass to rustc, so register that here. Eventually this flag\n        // will simply not be needed when the behavior is stabilized in the Rust\n        // compiler itself.\n        if *panic == PanicStrategy::Abort || *panic == PanicStrategy::ImmediateAbort {\n            cmd.arg(\"-Z\").arg(\"panic-abort-tests\");\n        }\n    } else if test {\n        cmd.arg(\"--cfg\").arg(\"test\");\n    }\n\n    cmd.args(&features_args(unit));\n    cmd.args(&check_cfg_args(unit));\n\n    let meta = build_runner.files().metadata(unit);\n    cmd.arg(\"-C\")\n        .arg(&format!(\"metadata={}\", meta.c_metadata()));\n    if let Some(c_extra_filename) = meta.c_extra_filename() {\n        cmd.arg(\"-C\")\n            .arg(&format!(\"extra-filename=-{c_extra_filename}\"));\n    }\n\n    if rpath {\n        cmd.arg(\"-C\").arg(\"rpath\");\n    }\n\n    cmd.arg(\"--out-dir\")\n        .arg(&build_runner.files().output_dir(unit));\n\n    unit.kind.add_target_arg(cmd);\n\n    add_codegen_linker(cmd, build_runner, unit, bcx.gctx.target_applies_to_host()?);\n\n    if incremental {\n        add_codegen_incremental(cmd, build_runner, unit)\n    }\n\n    let pkg_hint_mostly_unused = match hints.mostly_unused {\n        None => None,\n        Some(toml::Value::Boolean(b)) => Some(b),\n        Some(v) => {\n            unit_capped_warn(&format!(\n                \"ignoring unsupported value type ({}) for 'hints.mostly-unused', which expects a boolean\",\n                v.type_str()\n            ))?;\n            None\n        }\n    };\n    if profile_hint_mostly_unused\n        .or(pkg_hint_mostly_unused)\n        .unwrap_or(false)\n    {\n        if bcx.gctx.cli_unstable().profile_hint_mostly_unused {\n            cmd.arg(\"-Zhint-mostly-unused\");\n        } else {\n            if profile_hint_mostly_unused.is_some() {\n                // Profiles come from the top-level unit, so we don't use \u0060unit_capped_warn\u0060 here.\n                warn(\n                    \"ignoring 'hint-mostly-unused' profile option, pass \u0060-Zprofile-hint-mostly-unused\u0060 to enable it\",\n                )?;\n            } else if pkg_hint_mostly_unused.is_some() {\n                unit_capped_warn(\n                    \"ignoring 'hints.mostly-unused', pass \u0060-Zprofile-hint-mostly-unused\u0060 to enable it\",\n                )?;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    let strip = strip.into_inner();\n    if strip != StripInner::None {\n        cmd.arg(\"-C\").arg(format!(\"strip={}\", strip));\n    }\n\n    if unit.is_std {\n        // -Zforce-unstable-if-unmarked prevents the accidental use of\n        // unstable crates within the sysroot (such as \"extern crate libc\" or\n        // any non-public crate in the sysroot).\n        //\n        // RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP allows unstable features on stable.\n        cmd.arg(\"-Z\")\n
