### Dependency path-domain assessment

Six probe variants of the permanent parent `trust::tests::every_absolute_dependency_outside_the_written_tree_is_refused` ran with the real pinned Cargo on the project-owned plain copy at the maintained sweep layout on `2026-10-20`, with production, every test and every reason unchanged (`xtask/src/trust.rs` at `d7c9403d2cf27a345b151fae86fc92c7a106b3be13f98569f12d577baa8999f4`). Ordinary outside inputs are refused exactly under the raw output root and under a symlinked output root. The leaf’s P0 hypothesis is now an observed outcome: with a space in the written tree’s path, an outside input whose name ends in a backslash, followed by an in-tree prerequisite, was read as one escaped in-tree path; the inventory was **written where a refusal was due**, omitted the outside input and named a decoy blob. Outside inputs with spaces are refused, but under fragment names. A final prerequisite ending in a backslash makes the pinned Cargo refuse its own dependency record, so the inventory returns an error and writes nothing. This is a bounded assessment: no repair is claimed, and the ambiguity repair and the terminal-backslash control are separately owned below.

#### Actual producer records and outcomes

The pinned rustc writes each prerequisite of the first dependency rule with its spaces as backslash-space and every other byte literally, then one per-file phony target per line. The inventory’s reader, `dependency_files` in `xtask/src/trust.rs`, consumes a known raw or canonical scratch prefix, escaped the same way, before splitting the remainder at the next space. One first-rule text can therefore name two different prerequisite lists, and the reader keeps the in-tree reading. The retained compiler-output text replaces only the runtime repository root with a declared placeholder; the published receipts apply the same replacement to the fixture file contents, and the audit records both digests.

| Variant | Outside inputs | Output root | Cargo exit | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ordinary` | `a.txt`, `m.txt`, `z.txt` | `out` | 0 | refused: exact outside-tree refusals; no inventory |
| `prefix-collision` | `prefix\` | `prefix crates/b/src` | 101 | written twice where a refusal was due; the outside input omitted; the decoy blob named |
| `spaces` | `a with space.txt`, `m with space.txt`, `z with space.txt` | `out` | 101 | refused under fragment names; two fragments classified as missing blobs |
| `alias-ascii` | `a.txt`, `m.txt`, `z.txt` | `output-alias` | 0 | refused: exact outside-tree refusals under the symlinked root; the canonical inside input accepted |
| `alias-spaces` | `a with space.txt`, `m with space.txt`, `z with space.txt` | `output-alias` | 101 | refused under fragment names, as spaces |
| `terminal-backslashes` | `a\`, `m\`, `z\` | `out` | 101 | error: the pinned Cargo refuses its own dependency record; nothing written, no refusal list |

#### Measured defects

**D1, P0, observed; owner `M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.1.1.1`.** Reproduction: the `prefix-collision` variant names the outside input `<run>/prefix\` from an admitted include site, tracks `<tree>/crates/b/src/tree/data.txt` through a second admitted site, holds a decoy `data.txt` at the tree root with the same bytes, and writes into the output root `prefix crates/b/src`. The first rule reads `crates/b/src/lib.rs <run>/prefix\ crates/b/src/tree/data.txt` while the phony targets list `<run>/prefix\:` and `crates/b/src/tree/data.txt:` on separate lines. The escaped scratch prefix is `<run>/prefix\ crates/b/src/tree/`, so the reader consumes the outside input, the field separator and the tree prefix together and keeps the residue `data.txt`, the decoy. Both runs wrote an inventory whose `chk` unit lists the library root and the decoy digest only; after the outside payload changed, the artifact digest changed while the recorded inputs did not. The pinned Cargo’s own rewritten `libb.d` reads the same text as one escaped in-tree path, so its fingerprint tracks the decoy too: the encoding, not this reader alone, is ambiguous. Impact: inventory written on both runs; the outside input omitted; the decoy blob at the tree root recorded; the artifact digest changes while the recorded inputs do not; the identity claim is false while the gate passes. Preconditions: a space in the written tree path; a host file named by the prefix before that space with a trailing backslash; an in-tree prerequisite spelled by the rest. Safe next repair: refusal, never a cleverer split: read the per-file phony targets as the line-delimited prerequisite list, require the first rule to agree, refuse any residual backslash outside the known prefixes naming the raw record, keep the spaced and line-broken scratch-root controls passing.

**D2, P1; same owner.** Reproduction: the `spaces` and `alias-spaces` variants name `a with space.txt`, `m with space.txt` and `z with space.txt` outside the tree; rustc writes each as `<run>/external/a\ with\ space.txt`. An outside prerequisite is split at each escaped space because only the known scratch prefixes are consumed intact. Outcome: refused, but under the fragments a-backslash, m-backslash, z-backslash, space.txt and with-backslash; the relative fragments are classified as missing blobs. The literal oracle expected the three complete paths. The outcome stays a refusal, so no inventory was written, but the diagnostics are false. Repair: the same refusal rule names the raw record text.

**D3, P2; owner `M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.1.1.2`.** Reproduction: the `terminal-backslashes` variant names `a\`, `m\` and `z\` outside the tree; rustc writes the rule ending in a literal backslash. The pinned Cargo refuses a dependency record whose final prerequisite ends in a backslash before the inventory reads anything: `error: could not parse/generate dep info at: <repository-root>/target/mutation-sweep/tree/target/trust-tests/absolute-dependency-refusals/out/target/chk/release/deps/b-20572edba3a82d76.d`. Outcome: the inventory returns the build error; nothing written; neither a written nor a refused outcome. Next: retain the exact rejecting constraint as a permanent control; decide whether the error is reported as a refusal.

Positive findings: ordinary outside inputs are refused exactly under the raw output root; under a symlinked output root rustc spells the first target with the raw alias and the manifest-reached inside input with the canonical root; the reader strips either, accepts the inside input and refuses the outside inputs exactly; the raw/canonical output-root geometry is not implicated in D1, D2 or D3. The literal oracle derives every expected refusal from the declared input names, so a passing variant is a complete refusal list and not a containment.

#### Restoration and continuity

All1156 regular inputs of the main tree restore against the probe’s manifest, by the probe’s own check and by a fresh re-derivation with `scripts/trust_adequacy.py --check-inputs`; the one Gitlink stays opaque pin metadata. The plain copy restores against the same manifest with the maintained `regular_input` reader and borrowed index identities. The production source digest `d7c9403d2cf27a345b151fae86fc92c7a106b3be13f98569f12d577baa8999f4` is the committed one; the reason file is unchanged; nothing under `xtask/` is staged. The staged seal of the literal refusal witness is byte for byte its leaf as the input commit held it, with one new index row, and all335 earlier archives are exact. The audit rejects 28 altered receipts, among them a refused outcome claimed for the collision, a dropped phony target, a false decoy digest, exact refusals claimed for the spaced variant, a parsed record claimed for the terminal backslash and a modified restoration. Four task states are reconstructible from the input commit by exact deltas. No Rust, test or reason changes, so the focused tier is not required by this commit; normal commit hooks remain binding.

#### Executable assessment adapters

Prepare the repository-local environment in `TOOLBOX.md`. The probe refreshes the plain copy from the retained manifest, substitutes each variant into the copy’s parent, runs the exact Cargo command, captures the dependency records and outcomes, restores the copy and checks the main inputs. The audit re-derives every claim above from the retained receipts and rejects the altered ones; the remaining adapters write the records and the book. Host toolchain and operating-system dependencies are necessary read-only inputs. Scripts are historical recipes for these exact inputs, not permission to alter the fixture exception or maintained external repositories.

<details>
<summary>Exact dependency path-domain probe.py</summary>

~~~python
from pathlib import Path
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import hashlib, importlib.util, json, os, re, shutil, stat, subprocess, tempfile, time

root = Path.cwd().resolve()
out = root / 'target/dependency-path-domain-assessment'
copy = root / 'target/mutation-sweep/tree'
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('adequacy', root / 'scripts/trust_adequacy.py')
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(m)
snapshot = m.load_input_snapshot((out / 'main-inputs.json').read_bytes())
source = (root / 'xtask/src/trust.rs').read_text()
start = source.index('    #[test]\n    fn every_absolute_dependency_outside_the_written_tree_is_refused()')
end = source.index("    fn package_item<'a>", start)
body = source[start:end]
name = 'trust::tests::every_absolute_dependency_outside_the_written_tree_is_refused'
command = ['cargo', 'test', '--locked', '--offline', '-q', '-p', 'xtask', name, '--', '--exact']
env = dict(os.environ, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=str(root / 'target/mutation-sweep/target'),
           ARCHOGEN_SWEEP_SOURCE=str(root))
sha = lambda raw: hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
norm = lambda value: value.replace(str(root), '<repository-root>')

def save(path, value):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n')

def safe(path):
    assert path.is_relative_to(root / 'target')
    for part in [path, *path.parents]:
        if part == root:
            break
        assert not part.is_symlink(), str(part)
        if part.exists():
            assert part.stat().st_dev == root.stat().st_dev, str(part)

safe(copy)
assert not (copy / '.git').exists() and not (copy / '.git').is_symlink()
copy.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for relative, entry in snapshot['regular'].items():
    src, dst = root / relative, copy / relative
    assert sha(src.read_bytes()) == entry['sha256']
    safe(dst)
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=dst.parent, delete=False) as handle:
        temporary = Path(handle.name)
    try:
        shutil.copy2(src, temporary)
        temporary.replace(dst)
    finally:
        temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
assert (copy / 'xtask/src/trust.rs').read_text() == source
print('Plain copy refreshed:', len(snapshot['regular']), 'regular inputs; no copied Git index; one opaque gitlink omitted', flush=True)

def variant(kind):
    text = body
    inputs = [('FIRST', 'a.txt', 'first external input\n'),
              ('MIDDLE', 'm.txt', 'middle external input\n'),
              ('LAST', 'z.txt', 'last external input\n')]
    additions = []
    output = 'out'
    if kind in ('spaces', 'alias-spaces'):
        inputs = [(constant, file.replace('.txt', ' with space.txt'), data) for constant, file, data in inputs]
    if kind == 'terminal-backslashes':
        inputs = [(constant, file[0] + '\\', data) for constant, file, data in inputs]
    if kind == 'prefix-collision':
        text = text.replace('.join(name)\n            .join("external");', '.join(name);', 1)
        inputs = [('OUTSIDE', 'prefix\\', 'outside first payload\n')]
        additions = [('crates/b/src/tree/data.txt', 'held decoy bytes\n'), ('data.txt', 'held decoy bytes\n')]
        inside = 'pub const INSIDE: &str = include_str!("tree/data.txt");'
        output = 'prefix crates/b/src'
    elif kind.startswith('alias-'):
        additions = [('crates/b/src/inside.txt', 'inside tracked input\n')]
        inside = 'pub const INSIDE: &str = include_str!(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/src/inside.txt"));'
        output = 'output-alias'
    if additions:
        text = text.replace('let lines: Vec<_>', 'let mut lines: Vec<_>', 1)
        text = text.replace('        let admissions: String', '        lines.push(' + json.dumps(inside) + '.to_owned());\n        let admissions: String', 1)
        extra = ', '.join('(' + json.dumps(path) + ', ' + json.dumps(data) + '.to_owned())' for path, data in additions)
        old = '&[("trust/roots.eadl", format!("{ROOTS}{admissions}"))]'
        assert text.count(old) == 1
        text = text.replace(old, '&[("trust/roots.eadl", format!("{ROOTS}{admissions}")), ' + extra + ']', 1)
    array = '        let inputs = [\n' + ''.join('            (' + ', '.join(json.dumps(x) for x in row) + '),\n' for row in inputs) + '        ];'
    text, n = re.subn(r'        let inputs = \[.*?\n        \];', lambda _: array, text, count=1, flags=re.S)
    assert n == 1
    run = 'f.run()' if output == 'out' else 'f.run_into(' + json.dumps(output) + ')'
    prefix = ''
    if kind.startswith('alias-'):
        prefix = '''        let physical = f.base.join("physical-output");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&physical).unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&physical, f.base.join("output-alias")).unwrap();
'''
    if kind == 'prefix-collision':
        prefix += '        let first = ' + run + ';\n'
        prefix += '        let inventory = f.base.join(' + json.dumps(output + '/trust-dependencies.json') + ');\n'
        prefix += '        if inventory.exists() { std::fs::copy(&inventory, f.base.join("first-inventory.json")).unwrap(); }\n'
        prefix += '        std::fs::write(external.join("prefix\\\\"), "outside second payload changed\\n").unwrap();\n'
        prefix += '        let second = ' + run + ';\n'
        prefix += '        if inventory.exists() { std::fs::copy(&inventory, f.base.join("second-inventory.json")).unwrap(); }\n'
        prefix += '        let shape = |value: &Outcome| match value { Outcome::Written(_) => "written", Outcome::Refused(_) => "refused" };\n'
        prefix += '        std::fs::write(f.base.join("observed-outcomes.txt"), format!("first={}\\nsecond={}\\n", shape(&first), shape(&second))).unwrap();\n'
        run = 'first'
    original = '        assert_eq!(refused(f.run()), expected);\n        assert!(!f.base.join("out/trust-dependencies.json").exists());'
    assert text.count(original) == 1
    text = text.replace(original, prefix + '        assert_eq!(refused(' + run + '), expected);\n        assert!(!f.base.join(' + json.dumps(output + '/trust-dependencies.json') + ').exists());', 1)
    return text, inputs, output

records = []
error = None
try:
    (out / 'qualified').mkdir()
    for kind in ['ordinary', 'prefix-collision', 'spaces', 'alias-ascii', 'alias-spaces', 'terminal-backslashes']:
        case = out / 'qualified' / kind
        assert not case.exists(), 'Do not overwrite completed case: ' + kind
        case.mkdir()
        changed, inputs, output = variant(kind)
        (case / 'parent.rs').write_text(changed)
        (copy / 'xtask/src/trust.rs').write_text(source[:start] + changed + source[end:])
        began = time.monotonic()
        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=copy, env=env, capture_output=True, timeout=600)
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - began
        (case / 'stdout.log').write_bytes(result.stdout)
        (case / 'stderr.log').write_bytes(result.stderr)
        base = copy / 'target/trust-tests/absolute-dependency-refusals'
        captured = {}
        for path in sorted(base.rglob('*.d')):
            if path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink():
                captured[str(path.relative_to(base))] = norm(path.read_text())
        for file in ['first-inventory.json', 'second-inventory.json', 'observed-outcomes.txt', output + '/trust-dependencies.json']:
            path = base / file
            if path.is_file():
                captured[file] = norm(path.read_text())
        held = {}
        if (base / 'repo/.git').is_dir():
            tracked = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'ls-files', '-z'], cwd=base / 'repo').decode().strip('\0').split('\0')
            held = {file: (base / 'repo' / file).read_text() for file in tracked}
        row = dict(case=kind, command=command, exit_code=result.returncode, elapsed_seconds=elapsed,
                   oracle='Complete literal outside-input refusals derived from the declared filenames, plus no inventory.',
                   inputs=inputs, output=output, source_sha256=sha((copy / 'xtask/src/trust.rs').read_bytes()),
                   parent_sha256=sha(changed.encode()), stdout=norm(result.stdout.decode()), stderr=norm(result.stderr.decode()),
                   captured=captured, fixture_files=held,
                   fixture_commit=subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], cwd=base / 'repo', text=True).strip() if held else None)
        save(case / 'record.json', row)
        records.append(row)
        save(out / 'qualified-results.json', records)
        print(kind + ': Cargo exit ' + str(result.returncode) + '; ' + str(len(captured)) + ' captured dependency/outcome files; %.2fs' % elapsed, flush=True)
except BaseException as caught:
    error = caught
finally:
    (copy / 'xtask/src/trust.rs').write_text(source)
    subprocess.run(['python3', '-I', '-B', 'scripts/trust_adequacy.py', '--check-inputs', str(out.relative_to(root) / 'main-inputs.json'),
                    '--output', str(out.relative_to(root) / 'main-restoration.json')], cwd=root, check=True)
    entries = [(name, {'index_mode': entry['index_mode'], 'index_oid': entry['index_oid']}) for name, entry in snapshot['regular'].items()]
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
        actual = dict(pool.map(lambda item: m.regular_input(copy, item), entries))
    assert actual == snapshot['regular']
    save(out / 'copy-restoration.json', dict(status='restored', regular_count=len(actual),
         qualification='Plain-copy bytes/modes checked with maintained regular_input and borrowed main index identities; no copied index or submodule-content claim.',
         manifest_sha256=sha((out / 'main-inputs.json').read_bytes())))
    print('All original/copied regular inputs restored:', len(actual), flush=True)
if error is not None:
    raise error
~~~

<summary>Exact dependency path-domain audit.py</summary>

~~~python
from pathlib import Path
import copy, hashlib, json, re, subprocess

out = Path('target/dependency-path-domain-assessment'); B = chr(96)
root = Path.cwd().resolve(); tag = '<repository-root>'
base = tag + '/target/mutation-sweep/tree/target/trust-tests/absolute-dependency-refusals'
exits = {'ordinary': 0, 'prefix-collision': 101, 'spaces': 101, 'alias-ascii': 0, 'alias-spaces': 101, 'terminal-backslashes': 101}
order = list(exits)
parent = 'trust::tests::every_absolute_dependency_outside_the_written_tree_is_refused'
command = ['cargo', 'test', '--locked', '--offline', '-q', '-p', 'xtask', parent, '--', '--exact']
source_sha = 'd7c9403d2cf27a345b151fae86fc92c7a106b3be13f98569f12d577baa8999f4'
decoy_sha = hashlib.sha256(b'held decoy bytes\n').hexdigest()
d_key = 'out/target/chk/release/deps/b-20572edba3a82d76.d'
alias_key = 'physical-output/target/chk/release/deps/b-20572edba3a82d76.d'
prefix_key = 'prefix crates/b/src/target/chk/release/deps/b-20572edba3a82d76.d'
prefix_lib_key = 'prefix crates/b/src/target/chk/release/libb.d'
seal_leaf = 'M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.1.0'; seal_file = 'docs/task-history/M3/' + seal_leaf + '.md'
externals = {'ordinary': ['a.txt', 'm.txt', 'z.txt'], 'spaces': ['a with space.txt', 'm with space.txt', 'z with space.txt'], 'terminal-backslashes': ['a\\', 'm\\', 'z\\']}
passed_text = 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed'
cargo_refusal = 'could not parse/generate dep info at: ' + base + '/' + d_key

def sha(raw): return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
def read(name): return json.loads((out / name).read_text())
def git(*args): return subprocess.check_output(['git', *args])
class Refused(AssertionError): pass
def need(condition, why):
    if not condition: raise Refused(why)
def normalise(value):
    if isinstance(value, str): return value.replace(str(root), tag)
    if isinstance(value, list): return [normalise(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict): return {k: normalise(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    return value
def rule(text): return text.split('\n')[0]
def escaped(path): return path.replace(' ', '\\ ')
def refusal(path, why): return 'trust-undeclared-input: ' + B + 'chk' + B + ' reads ' + B + path + B + ', ' + why

    return text

def judge(d):

    inside = base + '/physical-output/tree/crates/b/src/inside.txt'
    need(rule(a['captured'][alias_key]) == base + '/output-alias/target/chk/release/deps/b-20572edba3a82d76.d: crates/b/src/lib.rs ' + ext(externals['ordinary']) + ' ' + inside, 'alias-ascii: raw alias target, outside inputs, then the canonical inside input')
    need('# env-dep:CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=' + base + '/physical-output/tree/crates/b' in a['captured'][alias_key].split('\n'), 'alias-ascii: canonical manifest directory')
    need('std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&physical, f.base.join("output-alias")).unwrap();' in d['parent_texts']['qualified']['alias-ascii'], 'alias-ascii parent builds the alias')
    # spaces and alias-spaces: escaped spaces, literal backslashes, fragment refusals
    frag_left = [rendered(refusal(base + '/external/' + c + '\\', 'outside the written tree')) for c in 'amz'] + [rendered(refusal(f, 'which is not a blob of the commit')) for f in ['space.txt', 'with\\']]
    frag_right = [rendered(refusal(base + '/external/' + f, 'outside the written tree')) for f in externals['spaces']]
    for case, key in [('spaces', d_key), ('alias-spaces', alias_key)]:
        s = by[case]; text = s['captured'][key]

    c = d['copied']; need(c['status'] == 'restored' and c['regular_count'] == 1156 and c['manifest_sha256'] == d['manifest_sha256'], 'plain copy restored against the same manifest')
    need(d['manifest_regular'] == 1156 and d['manifest_gitlinks'] == 1 and d['manifest_has_seal'] and d['manifest_source_commit'] == d['head'], 'manifest covers the staged tree')

    arm('escaped-backslash-claimed:terminal-backslashes', lambda d: swap(d, 'terminal-backslashes', d_key, 'external/z\\\n', 'external/z\\\\\n'))
    arm('inside-input-dropped:alias-ascii', lambda d: swap(d, 'alias-ascii', alias_key, ' ' + base + '/physical-output/tree/crates/b/src/inside.txt\n', '\n'))
~~~

~~~python
    at = 0; chunks = []
    for change in entry['changes']:
~~~

### Dependency path-domain repair

The inventory’s dependency-record reader, `dependency_files` in `xtask/src/trust.rs`, is repaired by refusal on `2026-10-20` (production digest `9d17f39a35dba3a07d094c5374b0786a966bdf0705fb71a9201a5907872eb7ce`, source `93512551cf48fe29e8d577331a16947a72429b57ad7d1eaaa3d1229995b42f57`, previously `d7c9403d2cf27a345b151fae86fc92c7a106b3be13f98569f12d577baa8999f4`). The pinned rustc escapes a prerequisite’s spaces as backslash-space and writes every other byte literally, repeats the prerequisites in one rule per output, each followed by a blank line, lists one phony target per prerequisite on a line of its own, and writes its environment records after a blank line. The reader now marks only the written tree’s known raw and canonical prefixes at a prerequisite’s start before splitting the rule at spaces, refuses a backslash anywhere else, and requires the phony targets to re-spell exactly the list it read; a record that fails either test is returned as ambiguous with its raw first rule, and the inventory refuses the unit naming that rule. Never a cleverer split: the measured prefix collision is refused because its per-file targets spell the outside name and the in-tree prerequisite apart, and spaced outside inputs are refused because their escapes lie outside the known prefixes. The terminal-backslash control and the full dependency-block checkpoint remain separately owned.

#### Permanent controls and their actual records

Four real-Cargo controls replay the assessment’s variants with independent literal expectations, and one synthetic control holds the record grammar: the collision refused by its targets, the honest in-tree reading of the same rule text, backslashes inside and at the end of names, repeated rules with environment records read, and a dropped target, an extra target, a missing blank line, a rule spelled otherwise, reordered targets, a trailing line that is no environment record and an empty remainder refused. The scratch-root controls with a space, a line break, a carriage return, a backslash-space, a hash, a tick and a tab in the root keep passing. All1156 regular inputs of the main tree restore against the manifest captured before the sweep, by `scripts/trust_adequacy.py --check-inputs`; the one Gitlink stays opaque pin metadata. The plain copy restores against the same manifest with the maintained `regular_input` reader. The parent population grew from its retained 202 names by exactly the four added controls, listed identically in the main tree and in the copy; the baseline passes. The assessment leaf is sealed as its archive, and the longest sealed commit notes of the tree are routed verbatim below so the task directory stays under its byte ceiling. The audit rejects 20 altered receipts, among them a survived outcome, a foreign finishing parent, a dropped candidate, changed reasons, a foreign catalogue edit, a modified restoration, a collision record whose targets deny the ambiguity and a collapsed aliased root. The catalog builder in `xtask/src/catalog_build.rs` reads dependency records with its own space-splitting reader, which is outside this leaf; the dependency-block checkpoint `M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.2` owns that neighbouring consumer. The retained proofs pin the trust production as a premise in `xtask/mutation_sweep_tests.py`: the observer close proof, the caller-suffix constructor proof and the absolute-cwd proof, bind the environment-tail scope by the line that follows its loop, and bind the bounded Cargo path equivalences by loop identifiers that carry their line numbers. The production difference is confined to the reader, its result type and the dependency block of the unit reader, which read a compiler-written record after the build; the observer call, the argument collector, the absolute-cwd derivation, the environment loop and the Cargo path loops are unchanged, so each proof holds: the digests are re-bound, the scope now ends at the match on the reader’s result, the two loop identifiers are renumbered to their current lines, and every from-json and why text of the reasons file is byte for byte the committed one, as the revalidation record below retains.Rust and test changes land here, so the focused tier runs on the final staged tree before the commit; normal commit hooks remain binding.

#### Executable repair adapters

Prepare the repository-local environment in `TOOLBOX.md`. The edit adapters apply the exact source, catalogue and test changes to the input commit; the plan selects every current mutant overlapping a changed production line; the native runner executes the sweep under the write fence and proves restoration; the audit re-derives every claim above and rejects altered receipts; the remaining adapters route the notes, write the records and the book. Host toolchain and operating-system dependencies are necessary read-only inputs. Scripts are historical recipes for these exact inputs, not permission to alter maintained external repositories.

~~~python
"""Exact-text edits of xtask/src/trust.rs for leaf M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.1.1.1; each old text must occur once."""
from pathlib import Path
import sys

path = Path('xtask/src/trust.rs')
source = path.read_text()
edits = []

def edit(old, new):
    assert source.count(old) == 1, old[:120]
    edits.append((old, new))

OLD_READER = r'''/// Read rustc's first dependency rule, matching its known raw output target before interpreting separators.
/// A source path inside the written tree has the catalog's ASCII grammar; only its scratch prefix can contain
/// spaces or line breaks. Rustc escapes spaces in prerequisites, but writes line breaks literally. Consume each
/// known escaped prefix intact before splitting its path suffix. This is not a general Makefile parser.
fn dependency_files(
    text: &str,
    dependency_file: &Path,
    scratch: &str,
    canonical_scratch: &str,
) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    let target = format!("{}: ", dependency_file.display());
    let mut rest = text.strip_prefix(&target).ok_or_else(|| {
        format!(
            "{}: missing expected first dependency target",
            dependency_file.display()
        )
    })?;
    let prefixes = [
        scratch.replace(' ', "\\ "),
        canonical_scratch.replace(' ', "\\ "),
    ];
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    loop {
        rest = rest.trim_start_matches(' ');
        if rest.is_empty() || rest.starts_with(['\n', '\r']) {
            break;
        }
        let prefix = prefixes
            .iter()
            .find(|p| rest.starts_with(p.as_str()))
            .map_or(0, String::len);
        let suffix = &rest[prefix..];
        let end = prefix + suffix.find([' ', '\n', '\r']).unwrap_or(suffix.len());
        files.push(rest[..end].replace("\\ ", " "));
        rest = &rest[end..];
    }
    if files.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!(
            "{}: empty first dependency rule",
            dependency_file.display()
        ));
    }
    Ok(files)
}
'''

NEW_READER = r'''/// What one unit's dependency record names: its prerequisites, or the raw first rule and the way that text names
/// two prerequisite lists at once, which the inventory refuses rather than choosing one.
enum Prerequisites {
    Read(Vec<String>),
    Ambiguous { raw: String, why: &'static str },
}

/// Read rustc's first dependency rule, matching its known raw output target before interpreting separators.
/// A source path inside the written tree has the catalog's ASCII grammar; only its scratch prefix can contain
/// spaces or line breaks. Rustc escapes a prerequisite's spaces as backslash-space and writes every other byte
/// literally, repeats the prerequisites in one rule per output, each followed by a blank line, then lists one
/// phony target per prerequisite on a line of its own, then its `# env-dep:` records. A name ending in a backslash
/// followed by the next prerequisite spells the same text as one escaped path, so one rule can name two lists:
/// mark each known escaped prefix at a prerequisite's start before splitting at spaces, refuse a backslash anywhere
/// else, and require the phony targets to re-spell exactly the list read, naming the raw rule otherwise. This is
/// not a general Makefile parser.
fn dependency_files(
    text: &str,
    dependency_file: &Path,
    scratch: &str,
    canonical_scratch: &str,
) -> Result<Prerequisites, String> {
    let target = format!("{}: ", dependency_file.display());
    let rules = text.strip_prefix(&target).ok_or_else(|| {
        format!(
            "{}: missing expected first dependency target",
            dependency_file.display()
        )
    })?;
    // A path never holds a NUL, so a marked prefix is one token however many spaces or line breaks it holds.
    let marks = [("\0r", scratch), ("\0c", canonical_scratch)];
    let mut marked = format!(" {rules}");
    for (mark, prefix) in marks {
        marked = marked.replace(&format!(" {}", prefix.replace(' ', "\\ ")), &format!(" {mark}"));
    }
    let rule = marked.split_once('\n').map_or(marked.as_str(), |(rule, _)| rule);
    let mut raw = rule.to_owned();
    for (mark, prefix) in marks {
        raw = raw.replace(mark, &prefix.replace(' ', "\\ "));
    }
    let raw = raw[1..].to_owned();
    let rest = &rules[raw.len()..];
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    for token in rule.split(' ').filter(|t| !t.is_empty()) {
        let (prefix, suffix) = marks
            .iter()
            .find_map(|&(mark, prefix)| token.strip_prefix(mark).map(|s| (prefix, s)))
            .unwrap_or(("", token));
        if suffix.contains('\\') {
            return Ok(Prerequisites::Ambiguous {
                raw,
                why: "a backslash outside the written tree's prefixes",
            });
        }
        files.push(format!("{prefix}{suffix}"));
    }
    if files.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!(
            "{}: empty first dependency rule",
            dependency_file.display()
        ));
    }
    let phony: String = files
        .iter()
        .map(|f| format!("{}:\n", f.replace(' ', "\\ ")))
        .collect();
    let repeated = format!(": {raw}\n\n");
    let agreed = rest
        .strip_prefix("\n\n")
        .and_then(|t| t.rsplit(&repeated).next())
        .and_then(|t| t.strip_prefix(&phony))
        .is_some_and(|env| env.lines().all(|l| l.starts_with("# env-dep:")));
    if !agreed {
        return Ok(Prerequisites::Ambiguous {
            raw,
            why: "its per-file targets spell the prerequisites otherwise",
        });
    }
    Ok(Prerequisites::Read(files))
}

UNIT_TESTS = r'''    /// One first-rule text can spell two prerequisite lists: the per-file targets decide, and a rule they do not
    /// re-spell, a backslash outside the known prefixes, or a line after them that is no environment record, is
    /// refused naming the raw rule (`M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.1.1.1`).
    #[test]
    fn an_ambiguous_dependency_record_is_refused_by_its_raw_rule() {
        let file = std::path::Path::new("out/b.d");
        let scratch = "/run/prefix crates/b/src/tree/";
        let record =
            |rule: &str, rest: &str| super::dependency_files(&format!("out/b.d: {rule}{rest}"), file, scratch, "/canonical/");
        let collision = "crates/b/src/lib.rs /run/prefix\\ crates/b/src/tree/data.txt";
        let targets = "its per-file targets spell the prerequisites otherwise";
        let backslash = "a backslash outside the written tree's prefixes";
        // The targets spell the outside name and the in-tree prerequisite apart: refused, never the decoy.
        assert_eq!(
            ambiguous(record(collision, "\n\ncrates/b/src/lib.rs:\n/run/prefix\\:\ncrates/b/src/tree/data.txt:\n").unwrap()),
            (collision.to_owned(), targets)
        );
        // The same rule whose targets spell one in-tree path is read as that path.
        assert_eq!(
            read(record(collision, "\n\ncrates/b/src/lib.rs:\n/run/prefix\\ crates/b/src/tree/data.txt:\n").unwrap()),
            ["crates/b/src/lib.rs", "/run/prefix crates/b/src/tree/data.txt"]
        );
        for (rule, why) in [
            ("a /ext/x\\ y.txt", backslash),
            ("a /ext/x\\y.txt", backslash),
            ("a /run/prefix\\ crates/b/src/tree/x\\y.txt", backslash),
        ] {
            let spelled: String = rule.split(' ').map(|t| format!("{t}:\n")).collect();
            assert_eq!(ambiguous(record(rule, &format!("\n\n{spelled}")).unwrap()), (rule.to_owned(), why), "{rule}");
        }
        for rest in [
            "\n\nout/libb.rlib: a b\n\na:\nb:\n# env-dep:X=1\n# env-dep:Y\n",
            "\n\nout/libb.rlib: a b\n\nout/libb.rmeta: a b\n\na:\nb:\n",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(read(record("a b", rest).unwrap()), ["a", "b"], "{rest:?}");
        }
        for rest in [
            "\n\na:\n",
            "\n\na:\nb:\nc:\n",
            "\na:\nb:\n",
            "\n\nout/libb.rlib: a c\n\na:\nb:\n",
            "\n\nout/libb.rlib: a b\n\nb:\na:\n",
            "\n\na:\nb:\n# env-dep X # env-dep:Y\n",
            "\n\na:\nb:\nextra\n",
            "",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(ambiguous(record("a b", rest).unwrap()), ("a b".to_owned(), targets), "{rest:?}");
        }
    }

            std::fs::create_dir_all(&external).unwrap();

                std::fs::write(external.join(file), contents).unwrap();
            }
            let mut rule = vec!["crates/b/src/lib.rs".to_owned()];
            rule.extend(inputs.iter().map(|(_, file, _)| {
                external.join(file).display().to_string().replace(' ', "\\ ")
            }));
            if out != "out" {
                let physical = base.join("physical-output");
                std::fs::create_dir_all(&physical).unwrap();
                std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&physical, base.join(out)).unwrap();
                rule.push(
                    std::fs::canonicalize(&physical)
                        .unwrap()
                        .join("tree/crates/b/src/inside.txt")
                        .display()
                        .to_string(),
                );
            }
            let expected = format!(
                "trust-undeclared-input: `chk` reads `{}` ambiguously: a backslash outside the written tree's \
                 prefixes",
                rule.join(" ")
            );
            assert_eq!(refused(f.run_into(out)), [expected], "{name}");
            assert!(!f.base.join(out).join("trust-dependencies.json").exists());
        }
    }

    /// A symbolic link as the output root: rustc spells an in-tree input by the raw root when its site names it so
    /// and by the canonical root when the manifest directory reaches it. Both are the written tree, the input is
    /// accepted once, and the three outside inputs are refused exactly.
    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn a_symbolic_output_root_accepts_raw_and_canonical_in_tree_inputs() {
        crate::trust_test_process::bounded!(
            a_symbolic_output_root_accepts_raw_and_canonical_in_tree_inputs
        );
        let name = "dependency-alias-refusals";
        let base = real_root().join("target/trust-tests").join(name);
        let external = base.join("external");
        let inputs = [
            ("FIRST", "a.txt", "first external input\n"),
            ("MIDDLE", "m.txt", "middle external input\n"),
            ("LAST", "z.txt", "last external input\n"),
        ];
        let mut lines: Vec<_> = inputs
            .iter()
            .map(|(constant, file, _)| {
                format!(
                    "pub const {constant}: &str = include_str!({:?});",
                    external.join(file).to_str().unwrap()
                )
            })
            .collect();
        lines.push(format!(
            "pub const RAW: &str = include_str!({:?});",
            base.join("output-alias/tree/crates/b/src/inside.txt")
                .to_str()
                .unwrap()
        ));
        lines.push("pub const CANONICAL: &str = include_str!(concat!(env!(\"CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR\"), \"/src/inside.txt\"));".to_owned());
        let admissions: String = lines
            .iter()
            .map(|line| admit("crates/b/src/lib.rs", "include_str", line))
            .collect();
        let f = two_roots(
            name,
            "fn main() {}\n",
            &(lines.join("\n") + "\n"),
            &[
                ("trust/roots.eadl", format!("{ROOTS}{admissions}")),
                ("crates/b/src/inside.txt", "inside tracked input\n".to_owned()),
            ],
        );
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&external).unwrap();
        for (_, file, contents) in inputs {
            std::fs::write(external.join(file), contents).unwrap();
        }
        let physical = base.join("physical-output");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&physical).unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&physical, base.join("output-alias")).unwrap();
        let expected: Vec<_> = inputs
            .iter()
            .map(|(_, file, _)| {
                format!(
                    "trust-undeclared-input: `chk` reads `{}`, outside the written tree",
                    external.join(file).display()
                )
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(refused(f.run_into("output-alias")), expected);
        assert!(!f.base.join("output-alias/trust-dependencies.json").exists());
    }
~~~

~~~python
"""Mark and unmark the two known prefixes by explicit calls: a loop over a two-element array has an equivalent
narrowing, and the contract keeps the equivalence reasons unchanged."""
from pathlib import Path
path = Path('xtask/src/trust.rs'); source = path.read_text()
old = '''    // A path never holds a NUL, so a marked prefix is one token however many spaces or line breaks it holds.
    let marks = [("\\0r", scratch), ("\\0c", canonical_scratch)];
    let mut marked = format!(" {rules}");
    for (mark, prefix) in marks {
        marked = marked.replace(
            &format!(" {}", prefix.replace(' ', "\\\\ ")),
            &format!(" {mark}"),
        );
    }
    let rule = marked
        .split_once('\\n')
        .map_or(marked.as_str(), |(rule, _)| rule);
    let mut raw = rule.to_owned();
    for (mark, prefix) in marks {
        raw = raw.replace(mark, &prefix.replace(' ', "\\\\ "));
    }
    let raw = raw[1..].to_owned();
    let rest = &rules[raw.len()..];
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    for token in rule.split(' ').filter(|t| !t.is_empty()) {
        let (prefix, suffix) = marks
            .iter()
            .find_map(|&(mark, prefix)| token.strip_prefix(mark).map(|s| (prefix, s)))
            .unwrap_or(("", token));
'''
new = '''    // A path never holds a NUL, so a marked prefix is one token however many spaces or line breaks it holds.
    let raw_prefix = scratch.replace(' ', "\\\\ ");
    let canonical_prefix = canonical_scratch.replace(' ', "\\\\ ");
    let marked = format!(" {rules}")
        .replace(&format!(" {raw_prefix}"), " \\0r")
        .replace(&format!(" {canonical_prefix}"), " \\0c");
    let rule = marked
        .split_once('\\n')
        .map_or(marked.as_str(), |(rule, _)| rule);
    let raw = rule
        .replace("\\0r", &raw_prefix)
        .replace("\\0c", &canonical_prefix)[1..]
        .to_owned();
    let rest = &rules[raw.len()..];
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    for token in rule.split(' ').filter(|t| !t.is_empty()) {
        let (prefix, suffix) = [("\\0r", scratch), ("\\0c", canonical_scratch)]
            .into_iter()
            .find_map(|(mark, prefix)| token.strip_prefix(mark).map(|s| (prefix, s)))
            .unwrap_or(("", token));
'''
assert source.count(old) == 1
path.write_text(source.replace(old, new, 1)); print('marks restructured')
~~~

~~~python
"""Re-bind the catalogue entry that quotes the reader: its `from` is the new function, its `to` the naive reader."""
from pathlib import Path
import re
source = Path('xtask/src/trust.rs').read_text()
start = source.index('fn dependency_files(\n')
end = source.index('\n}\n', start) + 3
function = source[start:end]
assert function.count('fn ') == 1 and function.endswith('    Ok(Prerequisites::Read(files))\n}\n')
indented = ''.join(('    ' + line if line else line) + '\n' for line in function.rstrip('\n').split('\n'))
catalogue = Path('xtask/mutations.txt').read_text()
head = 'mutation trust-dependency-first-physical-line\n'
assert catalogue.count(head) == 1
at = catalogue.index(head)
entry_end = catalogue.index('\nend\n', at) + 5
entry = catalogue[at:entry_end]
old_from = entry[entry.index('from\n') + 5:entry.index('\nto\n') + 1]
assert old_from.startswith('    fn dependency_files(\n') and old_from.count('    fn dependency_files(') == 1
old_to = entry[entry.index('\nto\n') + 4:entry.index('\nend\n') + 1]
new_to = '''    fn dependency_files(
        text: &str,
        dependency_file: &Path,
        scratch: &str,
        canonical_scratch: &str,
    ) -> Result<Prerequisites, String> {
        let _ = (dependency_file, scratch, canonical_scratch);
        let first = text
            .lines()
            .find(|line| !line.is_empty() && !line.starts_with("# env-dep:"))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let rest = first.split_once(": ").map(|(_,rest)| rest).unwrap_or_default();
        Ok(Prerequisites::Read(rest.split(' ').filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).map(|s| s.replace("\\\\ ", " ")).collect()))
    }
'''
new_entry = entry.replace(old_from, indented, 1).replace(old_to, new_to, 1)
assert new_entry.count('from\n') == 1 and new_entry.count('\nto\n') == 1
# The source must hold the exact `from` once, four spaces of catalogue indentation removed.
dedented = ''.join(line[4:] + '\n' if line.startswith('    ') else line + '\n' for line in indented.rstrip('\n').split('\n'))
assert source.count(dedented) == 1, 'from text must occur once in the source'
Path('xtask/mutations.txt').write_text(catalogue[:at] + new_entry + catalogue[entry_end:])
print('catalogue entry re-bound;', len(indented.splitlines()), 'from lines;', len(new_to.splitlines()), 'to lines')
~~~

~~~python
from pathlib import Path
import difflib, hashlib, importlib.util, json, subprocess

def sha(raw): return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('adequacy', 'scripts/trust_adequacy.py'); m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)

source = Path(file).read_bytes(); before = (out / 'source-before.rs').read_bytes()
assert before == subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', 'HEAD:' + file])

m.verify_listing(actual, listing, file, scope); (out / 'listing.log').write_text(actual)
old_lines = before.decode().split('\n'); new_lines = source.decode().split('\n')
first, last = scope
changed = []
for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, old_lines, new_lines, autojunk=False).get_opcodes():
    if tag == 'equal': continue
    lo, hi = max(j1, first), min(j2 if j2 > j1 else j1 + 1, last)
    if lo < hi: changed.append([lo, hi])
selected = [c for c in raw if any(m.overlaps(span, c['span']) for span in changed)]
production = source.split(b'#[cfg(test)]', 1)[0]
plan = dict(schema='archogen-dependency-path-domain-repair/1', status='planning-only', scope='Every current mutant overlapping a production line changed by the ambiguity repair; full current parent population; intended finishing kills required.',
            file=file, base_commit=subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip(), source_sha256=sha(source), production_sha256=sha(production),
            production_range=scope, listed_count=len(raw), changed_spans=changed, candidates=selected, equivalents=[],
            equivalents_sha256=sha(Path('xtask/trust.equivalents').read_bytes()), catalogue_sha256=sha(Path('xtask/mutations.txt').read_bytes()))
(out / 'plan.json').write_text(json.dumps(plan, indent=2) + '\n')
ops = {}
for c in selected: ops[c['operator']] = ops.get(c['operator'], 0) + 1
print('discovery', len(raw), 'scope', scope, 'changed spans', changed, 'selected', len(selected), ops)
for c in selected: print(' ', c['id'], json.dumps(c['original'].strip()[:90]), '->', json.dumps(c['replacement'].strip()[:90]))
~~~

~~~python
"""Re-derive every claim of the dependency path-domain repair from retained receipts, and reject altered ones."""
from pathlib import Path
import copy, difflib, hashlib, importlib.util, json, os, re, subprocess

out = Path('target/dependency-path-domain-repair'); file = 'xtask/src/trust.rs'; root = Path.cwd(); B = chr(96)
def sha(raw): return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
def read(name): return json.loads((out / name).read_text())
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('adequacy', 'scripts/trust_adequacy.py'); m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
env = dict(os.environ, CARGO_HOME=str(root / 'target/cargo-home'), TMPDIR=str(root / 'target/tmp'))
CONTROLS = ['dependency_information_requires_its_known_nonempty_target', 'an_ambiguous_dependency_record_is_refused_by_its_raw_rule',
            'cargo_dependency_information_retains_actual_source_paths', 'cargo_dependency_environment_normalizes_escaped_scratch_paths',
            'dependency_environment_uses_the_canonical_encoded_prefix', 'every_absolute_dependency_outside_the_written_tree_is_refused',
            'a_trailing_backslash_before_an_in_tree_prerequisite_is_refused_as_ambiguous', 'outside_inputs_with_spaces_are_refused_by_their_raw_rule',
            'a_symbolic_output_root_accepts_raw_and_canonical_in_tree_inputs']
ADDED = ['a_symbolic_output_root_accepts_raw_and_canonical_in_tree_inputs', 'a_trailing_backslash_before_an_in_tree_prerequisite_is_refused_as_ambiguous',
         'an_ambiguous_dependency_record_is_refused_by_its_raw_rule', 'outside_inputs_with_spaces_are_refused_by_their_raw_rule']
TESTS = 'target/trust-tests'
FIXTURES = {  # control fixture: (base directory, output root, dependency-record directory relative to the base)
    'prefix-collision': ('dependency-prefix-collision', 'prefix crates/b/src', 'prefix crates/b/src/target/chk/release/deps'),
    'spaces': ('dependency-spaced-refusals', 'out', 'out/target/chk/release/deps'),
    'alias-spaces': ('dependency-spaced-alias-refusals', 'output-alias', 'physical-output/target/chk/release/deps'),
    'alias': ('dependency-alias-refusals', 'output-alias', 'physical-output/target/chk/release/deps'),
}

def esc(path): return path.replace(' ', '\\ ')

def model_reader(text, dependency_file, scratch, canonical):
    """An independent model of the repaired reading, for cross-checking the retained records only."""
    rules = text[len(dependency_file + ': '):]; assert text.startswith(dependency_file + ': ')
    marked = (' ' + rules).replace(' ' + esc(scratch), ' \0r').replace(' ' + esc(canonical), ' \0c')
    rule = marked.split('\n', 1)[0]; raw = rule.replace('\0r', esc(scratch)).replace('\0c', esc(canonical))[1:]; rest = rules[len(raw):]
    files = []
    for token in [t for t in rule.split(' ') if t]:
        prefix, suffix = ('', token)
        for mark, p in [('\0r', scratch), ('\0c', canonical)]:
            if token.startswith(mark): prefix, suffix = p, token[len(mark):]; break
        if '\\' in suffix: return ('ambiguous', raw, "a backslash outside the written tree's prefixes")
        files.append(prefix + suffix)
    phony = ''.join(esc(f) + ':\n' for f in files); repeated = ': ' + raw + '\n\n'
    tail = rest[2:] if rest.startswith('\n\n') else None
    if tail is not None: tail = tail.rsplit(repeated, 1)[-1]
    if tail is None or not tail.startswith(phony): return ('ambiguous', raw, 'its per-file targets spell the prerequisites otherwise')
    after = tail[len(phony):]
    if after and not (after.startswith('\n') and all(l.startswith('# env-dep:') for l in after[1:].splitlines())):
        return ('ambiguous', raw, 'its per-file targets spell the prerequisites otherwise')
    return ('read', raw, files)

def collect():
    ctx = {}
    ctx['source'] = Path(file).read_bytes(); ctx['before'] = (out / 'source-before.rs').read_bytes()
    ctx['plan'] = read('plan.json'); ctx['execution'] = read('execution.json'); ctx['measurement'] = read('measurement.json')
    ctx['head'] = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip()
    ctx['head_source'] = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', ctx['head'] + ':' + file])
    ctx['script'] = Path('scripts/mutation_sweep.sh').read_text()
    ctx['listing'] = subprocess.check_output(['bash', 'scripts/mutation_sweep.sh', file, '--package', 'xtask', '--list'], text=True)
    ctx['retained_listing'] = (out / 'listing.log').read_text()
    ctx['log'] = (out / 'native.log').read_text(); ctx['rc'] = int((out / 'native.exit').read_text())
    ctx['names'] = (out / 'parent-list.log').read_text(); ctx['old_names'] = (out / 'parent-list-before.log').read_text(); ctx['copied_names'] = (out / 'copied-parent-list.log').read_text()
    ctx['equivalents'] = Path('xtask/trust.equivalents').read_bytes(); ctx['head_equivalents'] = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', ctx['head'] + ':xtask/trust.equivalents'])
    ctx['catalogue'] = Path('xtask/mutations.txt').read_text(); ctx['head_catalogue'] = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', ctx['head'] + ':xtask/mutations.txt'], text=True)
    ctx['mutate_log'] = (out / 'catalogue-entry.log').read_text(); ctx['baseline'] = (out / 'parent-baseline.log').read_text()
    ctx['original_restoration'] = read('original-restoration.json'); ctx['inputs'] = read('inputs-before.json'); ctx['copy_restoration'] = read('copy-restoration.json')
    ctx['protected'] = {name: Path(name).read_bytes() for name in ctx['execution']['protected']}
    ctx['revalidation'] = read('premise-revalidation.json')
    run = subprocess.run(['cargo', 'test', '--locked', '--offline', '-q', '-p', 'xtask', '--', *('trust::tests::' + c for c in CONTROLS), '--exact'], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    ctx['controls_rc'] = run.returncode; ctx['controls_log'] = run.stdout + run.stderr; (out / 'controls.log').write_text(ctx['controls_log'])
    records = {}
    for case, (base, output, deps) in FIXTURES.items():
        base_dir = root / TESTS / base; found = sorted((base_dir / deps).glob('b-*.d')); assert len(found) == 1, case
        # Rustc spells the record's own target by the raw output root, through a symbolic link where one stands.
        records[case] = dict(base=str(base_dir), output=output, dependency_file=str(base_dir / output / 'target/chk/release/deps' / found[0].name), text=found[0].read_text(),
                             inventory_written=(base_dir / output / 'trust-dependencies.json').exists(),
                             lib_rs=(base_dir / 'repo/crates/b/src/lib.rs').read_text(),
                             physical=str(os.path.realpath(base_dir / 'physical-output')) if (base_dir / 'physical-output').exists() else None)
    ctx['records'] = records
    return ctx

def verify(ctx):
    plan, execution, measurement = ctx['plan'], ctx['execution'], ctx['measurement']; source, before = ctx['source'], ctx['before']
    assert before == ctx['head_source'] and plan['base_commit'] == ctx['head'] == execution['base_commit']
    assert sha(source) == plan['source_sha256'] == execution['source_sha256'] and sha(source.split(b'#[cfg(test)]', 1)[0]) == plan['production_sha256']
    raw, listing, scope = m.discover(ctx['script'], source.decode()); assert len(raw) == plan['listed_count'] and scope == plan['production_range']
    m.verify_listing(ctx['listing'], listing, file, scope); assert ctx['listing'] == ctx['retained_listing']
    old_lines, new_lines = before.decode().split('\n'), source.decode().split('\n'); first, last = scope; changed = []
    for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, old_lines, new_lines, autojunk=False).get_opcodes():
        if tag == 'equal': continue

        if lo < hi: changed.append([lo, hi])

    selected = [c for c in raw if any(m.overlaps(span, c['span']) for span in changed)]; assert selected == plan['candidates'] and len(selected) == 37
    command = ['bash', 'scripts/mutation_sweep.sh', file, '--package', 'xtask', '--timeout', '600', '--filter=trust::', '--filter=trust_generated::', '--filter=trust_gate::',

    for c in selected: command += ['--only', c['id']]

    names = re.findall(r'^([\w:]+): test$', ctx['names'], re.M); old = re.findall(r'^([\w:]+): test$', ctx['old_names'], re.M)

    assert sorted(set(names) - set(old)) == ['trust::tests::' + n for n in ADDED]

            deleted_push = candidate['operator'] == 'stmt' and candidate['original'].strip() == 'files.push(format!("{prefix}{suffix}"));'
            assert row['outcome'] == 'unviable' and (narrowing or deleted_push) and row['detail'].startswith(' — error[E0'), row

    finishing = {}

    for old_id, new_id in renumbered.items(): assert expected_equivalents.count(old_id) == 10; expected_equivalents = expected_equivalents.replace(old_id, new_id)

    def entry(text): a = text.index('mutation trust-dependency-first-physical-line\n'); return text[a:text.index('\nend\n', a) + 5]
    assert ctx['head_catalogue'].replace(entry(ctx['head_catalogue']), entry(ctx['catalogue']), 1) == ctx['catalogue'] and sha(ctx['catalogue'].encode()) == plan['catalogue_sha256']
    current = entry(ctx['catalogue']); from_text = current[current.index('from\n') + 5:current.index('\nto\n') + 1]
    dedented = ''.join((line[4:] if line.startswith('    ') else line) + '\n' for line in from_text.rstrip('\n').split('\n'))
    assert source.decode().count(dedented) == 1 and dedented.startswith('fn dependency_files(\n') and 'Prerequisites::Read(files)' in dedented
    assert 'Result<Prerequisites, String>' in current[current.index('\nto\n'):] and 'Ok(Prerequisites::Read(' in current[current.index('\nto\n'):]
    assert '✓ trust-dependency-first-physical-line' in ctx['mutate_log'] and 'killed by trust::tests::cargo_dependency_information_retains_actual_source_paths' in ctx['mutate_log']
    assert 'mutate: OK' in ctx['mutate_log'] and 'mutate exit 0' in ctx['mutate_log']

        lines = text.split('\n'); first_rule = lines[0][len(record['dependency_file']) + 2:]; phony = [l[:-1] for l in lines if l.endswith(':') and not l.startswith('#')]

        else:

            expected = ["trust-undeclared-input: " + B + "chk" + B + " reads " + B + e + B + ", outside the written tree" for e in external]

        for line in [l for l in record['lib_rs'].splitlines() if 'include_str!' in l]: assert 'pub const ' in line
        normalized = lambda s: s.replace(str(root), '<repository-root>')
        records[case] = dict(output_root=output, raw_sha256=sha(text.encode()), record=normalized(text), first_rule=normalized(first_rule), phony_targets=[normalized(p) for p in phony],

                             inventory_written=record['inventory_written'], library_root=normalized(record['lib_rs']))

The terminal-backslash control and the full dependency-block checkpoint remain separately owned.',
                source_sha256=plan['source_sha256'], production_sha256=plan['production_sha256'], previous_source_sha256=sha(before), plan_sha256=execution['plan_sha256'], raw_discovery=len(raw), production_range=scope,
                changed_spans=changed, candidates=len(selected), native=measured, unviable=unviable, intended=intended, intended_finishing_counts=finishing, semantic_parents=206, previous_semantic_parents=202,

refuse('missing-outcome', lambda c: c.__setitem__('log', c['log'].replace(line + '\n', '', 1)))
refuse('wrong-strict-exit', lambda c: c.__setitem__('rc', 1))
refuse('wrong-source-binding', lambda c: c['plan'].__setitem__('source_sha256', '0' * 64))
refuse('dropped-candidate', lambda c: c['plan'].__setitem__('candidates', c['plan']['candidates'][1:]))
refuse('wrong-changed-span', lambda c: c['plan'].__setitem__('changed_spans', c['plan']['changed_spans'][1:]))
~~~

~~~python
"""Route the longest sealed commit-log notes of the M3 tree to the book verbatim, leaving compact pointers:
the task directory's byte ceiling must hold the closed repair leaf and its two log rows."""
from pathlib import Path
import json, re, subprocess
out = Path('target/dependency-path-domain-repair'); B = chr(96)
task = Path('docs/tasks/M3.md'); text = task.read_text()
assert text == (out / 'task-after-seal.md').read_text()
a = text.index('## Commit Log'); z = text.index('\n## ', a + 1)
rows = [l for l in text[a:z].split('\n') if l.startswith('| ' + B)]
sealed = set(re.findall(r'Status: ' + B + 'done' + B + r' — sealed in \[' + B + 'M3/(M3[^' + B + r']+)\.md' + B, text))
anchor = '../book/src/annex-trust-proofs.md#dependency-path-domain-repair-commit-note-routing'
pattern = re.compile(r'^\| (' + B + '[^' + B + ']+' + B + r') \| (' + B + '[^' + B + ']+' + B + r') \| (.*) \|$')
routes = []
for row in rows:
    if len(row.encode()) < 380 or 'routing' in row or 'ledger' in row or 'commit-records' in row: continue
    match = pattern.match(row); assert match, row
    leaf = match[1].strip(B)
    if leaf not in sealed: continue
    replacement = '| ' + match[1] + ' | ' + match[2] + ' | [Verbatim historical record](' + anchor + ') |'
    assert text.count(row + '\n') == 1
    routes.append(dict(leaf=leaf, original=row, replacement=replacement))
assert len(routes) == 21, len(routes)
for route in routes: text = text.replace(route['original'] + '\n', route['replacement'] + '\n', 1)
task.write_text(text); (out / 'task-after-routing.md').write_text(text)
(out / 'note-routing.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(anchor=anchor, date='2026-10-20', routes=routes), indent=2) + '\n')
freed = sum(len(r['original'].encode()) - len(r['replacement'].encode()) for r in routes)
print('routed', len(routes), 'sealed commit notes verbatim to the book;', freed, 'tree bytes freed')
~~~

~~~python
old_lines, new_lines = before.split('#[cfg(test)]', 1)[0].split('\n'), source.split('#[cfg(test)]', 1)[0].split('\n')
hunks = [(i1, i2, j1, j2) for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, old_lines, new_lines, autojunk=False).get_opcodes() if tag != 'equal']
tests = Path('xtask/mutation_sweep_tests.py'); text = tests.read_text(); head_tests = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', head + ':xtask/mutation_sweep_tests.py'], text=True)
assert head_tests.count("'xtask/src/trust.rs': '" + old_strict + "'") == 1 and head_tests.count('"' + old_prefix + '"') == 1 and head_tests.count("'xtask/src/trust.rs': '" + old_prefix + "'") == 1
old_stop = '        stop = "        for raw in dependency_files(&text, &d, &scratch, &canonical_scratch)? {"\n'
new_stop = '        stop = "        let raws = match dependency_files(&text, &d, &scratch, &canonical_scratch)? {"\n'
assert head_tests.count(old_stop) == 1 and source.count(new_stop[16:-2]) == 1
rebound = (head_tests.replace("'xtask/src/trust.rs': '" + old_strict + "'", "'xtask/src/trust.rs': '" + new_strict + "'", 1)
           .replace('"' + old_prefix + '"', '"' + new_prefix + '"', 1).replace("'xtask/src/trust.rs': '" + old_prefix + "'", "'xtask/src/trust.rs': '" + new_prefix + "'", 1)
           .replace(old_stop, new_stop, 1))
tests.write_text(rebound)
equivalents = Path('xtask/trust.equivalents'); head_equivalents = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', head + ':xtask/trust.equivalents'], text=True)
renumbered = {}
for header in ['for path in paths {', 'for spelling in std::iter::once(path).chain(canonical) {']:
    old_at = [i + 1 for i, l in enumerate(old_lines) if l.strip() == header]; new_at = [i + 1 for i, l in enumerate(new_lines) if l.strip() == header]
    assert len(old_at) == 1 and len(new_at) == 1; renumbered['__archogen_sweep_%d_' % old_at[0]] = '__archogen_sweep_%d_' % new_at[0]
current = head_equivalents
for old_id, new_id in renumbered.items():
    assert current.count(old_id) == 10 and new_id not in current; current = current.replace(old_id, new_id)
equivalents.write_text(current)
def records(text): return re.findall(r'^(from(?:-json)? .*)\n(to(?:-json)? .*)\n(why .*)$', text, re.M)
old_records, new_records = records(head_equivalents), records(current)
assert len(old_records) == len(new_records) == 23 and [(f, w) for f, _, w in old_records] == [(f, w) for f, _, w in new_records]
record = dict(file=file, base_commit=head, previous_production_sha256=old_prefix, production_sha256=new_prefix, previous_strict_production_sha256=old_strict, strict_production_sha256=new_strict,
              changed_production_hunks=[dict(old=[i1, i2], new=[j1, j2]) for i1, i2, j1, j2 in hunks],

                        'test_caller_suffix_prefix_requires_the_complete_pinned_constructor': 'production digest re-bound',
                        'IteratorTests absolute-cwd proof premises': 'production digest re-bound',
                        'EnvironmentTailTests.guarded_parts': 'the scope ends at the dependency call, now the match on its result; the loop text and every digest unchanged',
                        'IteratorTests.test_actual_cargo_path_end_loops_preserve_the_bounded_collections': 'the two loop identifiers renumbered to the loops’ current lines; from-json and why texts unchanged'},
              equivalents=dict(previous_sha256=sha(head_equivalents), sha256=sha(current), renumbered=renumbered, records=23, reasons_unchanged=True),
              sweep_tests=dict(previous_sha256=sha(head_tests), sha256=sha(rebound)),
              argument='The repair changes only the dependency-record reader, its result type and the dependency block of the unit reader, which read a compiler-written record after the build; the observer call, the argument collector, the absolute-cwd derivation, the environment loop and the Cargo path loops are unchanged, so each proof holds on the new production and is re-bound to its digest or its current line.')
(out / 'premise-revalidation.json').write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + '\n')
print('premises re-bound:', old_prefix[:12], '->', new_prefix[:12], ';', old_strict[:12], '->', new_strict[:12], '; stop marker; loops', renumbered)
~~~

### Dependency terminal-backslash control

The pinned Cargo's refusal of a dependency record whose final prerequisite ends in a backslash, D3 of the [path-domain assessment](#dependency-path-domain-assessment), is held as a permanent real-Cargo control on `2026-10-21`, with production unchanged (production digest `9d17f39a35dba3a07d094c5374b0786a966bdf0705fb71a9201a5907872eb7ce`, the pinned premise; source `555adc1630f9220d83412bff2848849e5264236bdcfe0fcd86488bf5b8aa5cdc`, previously `93512551cf48fe29e8d577331a16947a72429b57ad7d1eaaa3d1229995b42f57`; every changed line in the test module). The control `trust::tests::a_final_prerequisite_ending_in_a_backslash_is_the_builds_own_error` names three outside inputs `a\`, `m\` and `z\` from the library root's admitted `include_str!` sites, as the refusal parent names its ordinary inputs. The pinned rustc writes each backslash literally, so the first rule ends in a backslash; the pinned Cargo then refuses its own record as an internal error before the inventory reads anything. The run returns that error, writes no inventory and lists no refusal. The record rustc left is one the inventory's reader refuses as ambiguous, so the inventory does not rest on Cargo's refusal: a Cargo that stopped refusing would fail the control, and the reader would refuse the record.

#### The producer's own refusal

The control's fixture, under the ignored `target/trust-tests/` that the director's `2026-10-20` exception approves, keeps the record as rustc wrote it, the runtime repository root replaced by a declared placeholder:

```text
<repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/out/target/chk/release/deps/b-20572edba3a82d76.d: crates/b/src/lib.rs <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/a\ <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/m\ <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/z\

<repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/out/target/chk/release/deps/libb-20572edba3a82d76.rlib: crates/b/src/lib.rs <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/a\ <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/m\ <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/z\

<repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/out/target/chk/release/deps/libb-20572edba3a82d76.rmeta: crates/b/src/lib.rs <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/a\ <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/m\ <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/z\

crates/b/src/lib.rs:
<repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/a\:
<repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/m\:
<repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/z\:
```

Cargo's own output on that tree, `cargo build --lib --release --locked --offline --no-default-features -v -p b` run in the written tree with a scratch target directory, exit code 101, with its `Running` lines omitted:

```text
   Compiling b v0.1.0 (<repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/out/tree/crates/b)
error: could not parse/generate dep info at: <repository-root>/target/dependency-terminal-backslash-control/cargo-probe/target/release/deps/b-20572edba3a82d76.d

Caused by:
  malformed dep-info format, trailing \
note: this is an unexpected cargo internal error
note: we would appreciate a bug report: https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/
note: cargo 1.95.0 (f2d3ce0bd 2026-03-21)
```

The inventory's error carries the first error line, naming the record by its real path, and nothing else:

```text
`cargo build --lib --release --locked --offline --no-default-features --message-format=json -v -p b` failed: error: could not parse/generate dep info at: <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/out/target/chk/release/deps/b-20572edba3a82d76.d
```

Cargo's reader at the pinned commit, `cargo 1.95.0 (f2d3ce0bd 2026-03-21)`, takes a trailing backslash as the escape of the next whitespace-separated token and refuses the rule when none follows ([`parse_rustc_dep_info`](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/blob/f2d3ce0bd/src/cargo/core/compiler/fingerprint/dep_info.rs)):

```rust
            while let Some(s) = deps.next() {
                let mut file = s.to_string();
                while file.ends_with('\\') {
                    file.pop();
                    file.push(' ');
                    file.push_str(deps.next().ok_or_else(|| {
                        crate::util::internal("malformed dep-info format, trailing \\")
                    })?);
                }
                ret.files.entry(file.into()).or_default();
            }
```

and `rustc`'s work closure wraps that failure as the message the inventory carries ([`translate_dep_info` call](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/blob/f2d3ce0bd/src/cargo/core/compiler/mod.rs)):

```rust
            .with_context(|| {
                internal(format!(
                    "could not parse/generate dep info at: {}",
                    rustc_dep_info_loc.display()
                ))
            })?;
```

So three names ending in a backslash are joined by Cargo's reader into one name holding spaces, and the last backslash, with no token after it, is the refusal; the rule's text is the same whether a name ends in a backslash or a space was escaped, which is the ambiguity the [repair](#dependency-path-domain-repair) refuses on the inventory's side.

| Control | Output root | First rule as rustc wrote it | Cargo | Inventory | Model outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `terminal-backslashes` | `out` | `crates/b/src/lib.rs <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/a\ <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/m\ <repository-root>/target/trust-tests/dependency-terminal-backslashes/external/z\` | `malformed dep-info format, trailing \`, exit 101 | error, none written | ambiguous: a backslash outside the written tree's prefixes |

#### The decision: the error is an error

A build the pinned Cargo refuses is reported as the error it is, never as a refusal. A refusal is the inventory's judgment of a record it read: an input outside the written tree, an undeclared environment variable, a record whose text names two prerequisite lists. A record Cargo refused was never read by the inventory, and naming an input from it would mean reading past the producer's own refusal, or parsing Cargo's message for a cause the message does not establish. The gate fails on the error either way, nothing is written, and the outcome is unjudged rather than passed. The control pins both layers: the pinned Cargo's exact message naming the record, and the reader's refusal of the same record under its raw rule. The decision is recorded in the tree's decisions and in the trust chapter.

#### Restoration and continuity

No production line changed, so no edit sweep is owed by this leaf: the production digest is the sweep tests' pinned premise, the reasons (`xtask/trust.equivalents`), the catalogue (`xtask/mutations.txt`) and the sweep's own tests are byte for byte the committed ones, and the neighbouring sources are unchanged. The parent population grew from its retained 206 names by exactly the control, to 207, listed by the same command as the repair leaf's. The control and its nine companions pass by their exact names, live under the audit and in the retained logs. The audit rejects 21 altered receipts: `written-claimed`, `record-without-terminal-backslash`, `escaped-backslash-claimed`, `cargo-exit-zero`, `cargo-message-missing`, `cause-missing`, `internal-error-note-missing`, `foreign-cargo-version`, `inventory-error-foreign`, `controls-failed`, `live-controls-failed`, `control-alone-failed`, `parent-dropped`, `parent-foreign`, `control-renamed`, `production-changed`, `stale-pinned-premise`, `protected-changed`, `foreign-base-commit`, `span-in-production-claimed`, `reader-assertion-dropped`. The focused tier runs on the staged tree before the commit.

~~~python
            .iter()
~~~

~~~python
wrote, the pinned Cargo's own message, and the unchanged production, reasons and catalogue."""

import hashlib, json, os, re, subprocess, sys

out = Path('target/dependency-terminal-backslash-control'); file = 'xtask/src/trust.rs'; root = Path.cwd()
TESTS = 'target/trust-tests'; NAME = 'dependency-terminal-backslashes'
CONTROL = 'a_final_prerequisite_ending_in_a_backslash_is_the_builds_own_error'
CONTROLS = ['dependency_information_requires_its_known_nonempty_target', 'an_ambiguous_dependency_record_is_refused_by_its_raw_rule',
            'cargo_dependency_information_retains_actual_source_paths', 'cargo_dependency_environment_normalizes_escaped_scratch_paths',
            'dependency_environment_uses_the_canonical_encoded_prefix', 'every_absolute_dependency_outside_the_written_tree_is_refused',
            'a_trailing_backslash_before_an_in_tree_prerequisite_is_refused_as_ambiguous', 'outside_inputs_with_spaces_are_refused_by_their_raw_rule',
            'a_symbolic_output_root_accepts_raw_and_canonical_in_tree_inputs', CONTROL]
PROTECTED = ['xtask/trust.equivalents', 'xtask/mutations.txt', 'xtask/mutation_sweep_tests.py', 'xtask/src/trust_compiler.rs',
             'xtask/src/trust_compiler_observer.rs', 'xtask/src/catalog_build.rs', 'xtask/src/catalog_check.rs']
def sha(raw): return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
def production(text): return text.split('#[cfg(test)]', 1)[0]
env = dict(os.environ, CARGO_HOME=str(root / 'target/cargo-home'), TMPDIR=str(root / 'target/tmp'))

head = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip()
assert head == (out / 'base-commit.txt').read_text().strip()
source = Path(file).read_text(); before = (out / 'source-before.rs').read_text()
head_source = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', f'{head}:{file}'], text=True)
assert before == head_source, 'the retained source-before is the committed source'
# Every changed line lies in the test module: production is unchanged by construction.
test_line = before.index('\n#[cfg(test)]\n')
assert production(source) == production(before)
import difflib
changed = [(tag, i1, i2, j1, j2) for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, before.split('\n'), source.split('\n'), autojunk=False).get_opcodes() if tag != 'equal']
~~~
