~~~python
"""Re-derive every claim of the terminal-backslash control from retained receipts and a live run, and reject altered ones."""
from pathlib import Path
import copy, difflib, hashlib, json, os, re, subprocess

out = Path('target/dependency-terminal-backslash-control'); file = 'xtask/src/trust.rs'; root = Path.cwd()
def sha(raw): return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
def read(name): return json.loads((out / name).read_text())
def production(text): return text.split('#[cfg(test)]', 1)[0]
env = dict(os.environ, CARGO_HOME=str(root / 'target/cargo-home'), TMPDIR=str(root / 'target/tmp'))
BACKSLASH = "a backslash outside the written tree's prefixes"
BUILD = '`cargo build --lib --release --locked --offline --no-default-features --message-format=json -v -p b` failed: error: could not parse/generate dep info at: '

def esc(path): return path.replace(' ', '\\ ')

def model_reader(text, dependency_file, scratch, canonical):
    """An independent model of the repaired reading, for cross-checking the retained record only."""
    rules = text[len(dependency_file + ': '):]; assert text.startswith(dependency_file + ': ')
    marked = (' ' + rules).replace(' ' + esc(scratch), ' \0r').replace(' ' + esc(canonical), ' \0c')
    rule = marked.split('\n', 1)[0]; raw = rule.replace('\0r', esc(scratch)).replace('\0c', esc(canonical))[1:]; rest = rules[len(raw):]
    files = []
    for token in [t for t in rule.split(' ') if t]:
        prefix, suffix = ('', token)
        for mark, p in [('\0r', scratch), ('\0c', canonical)]:
            if token.startswith(mark): prefix, suffix = p, token[len(mark):]; break
        if '\\' in suffix: return ('ambiguous', raw, BACKSLASH)
        files.append(prefix + suffix)
    phony = ''.join(esc(f) + ':\n' for f in files); repeated = ': ' + raw + '\n\n'
    tail = rest[2:] if rest.startswith('\n\n') else None
    if tail is not None: tail = tail.rsplit(repeated, 1)[-1]
    if tail is None or not tail.startswith(phony): return ('ambiguous', raw, 'its per-file targets spell the prerequisites otherwise')
    after = tail[len(phony):]
    if after and not (after.startswith('\n') and all(l.startswith('# env-dep:') for l in after[1:].splitlines())):
        return ('ambiguous', raw, 'its per-file targets spell the prerequisites otherwise')
    return ('read', raw, files)

def collect():
    ctx = {'results': read('results.json')}
    ctx['source'] = Path(file).read_text(); ctx['before'] = (out / 'source-before.rs').read_text()
    ctx['head'] = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip()
    ctx['head_source'] = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', ctx['head'] + ':' + file], text=True)
    ctx['control_log'] = (out / 'control.log').read_text(); ctx['controls_log'] = (out / 'controls.log').read_text()
    ctx['names'] = (out / 'parent-list.log').read_text(); ctx['old_names'] = (out / 'parent-list-before.log').read_text()
    ctx['cargo_stderr'] = (out / 'cargo-probe/stderr.log').read_text(); ctx['cargo_exit'] = int((out / 'cargo-probe/exit.log').read_text().split()[-1])
    ctx['pinned'] = Path('xtask/mutation_sweep_tests.py').read_text()
    ctx['protected'] = {name: Path(name).read_bytes() for name in ctx['results']['protected']}
    ctx['head_protected'] = {name: subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', ctx['head'] + ':' + name]) for name in ctx['results']['protected']}
    fixture = ctx['results']['fixture']; base = Path(fixture['base'])
    found = sorted(p for p in (base / 'out/target/chk/release/deps').glob('b-*.d')); assert len(found) == 1, found
    ctx['record'] = dict(path=str(found[0]), text=found[0].read_text(), inventory_written=(base / 'out/trust-dependencies.json').exists(),
                         externals=sorted(p.name for p in (base / 'external').iterdir()), lib_rs=(base / 'repo/crates/b/src/lib.rs').read_text())
    # The live leg: the control and its nine companions, each by its exact name, re-run now.
    run = subprocess.run(['cargo', 'test', '--locked', '--offline', '-q', '-p', 'xtask', '--', *ctx['results']['controls'], '--exact'], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    ctx['live_rc'] = run.returncode; ctx['live_log'] = run.stdout + run.stderr; (out / 'controls-live.log').write_text(ctx['live_log'])
    return ctx

def verify(ctx):
    r = ctx['results']; source, before = ctx['source'], ctx['before']; control = r['control']
    assert r['schema'] == 'archogen-dependency-terminal-backslash-control/1' and r['base_commit'] == ctx['head'] and before == ctx['head_source']
    assert sha(source.encode()) == r['source_sha256'] and sha(before.encode()) == r['source_before_sha256']
    # Production is unchanged by construction: every changed line lies in the test module, and the pinned premise is the digest.
    assert production(source) == production(before) and sha(production(source).encode()) == r['production_sha256']
    first_test_line = before[:before.index('\n#[cfg(test)]\n')].count('\n') + 1; assert first_test_line == r['first_test_line']
    spans = [[i1, i2, j1, j2] for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, before.split('\n'), source.split('\n'), autojunk=False).get_opcodes() if tag != 'equal']
    assert spans == r['changed_spans'] and all(span[0] >= first_test_line for span in spans)
    assert ctx['pinned'].count("'xtask/src/trust.rs': '" + r['production_sha256'] + "'") >= 1 and sha(ctx['pinned'].encode()) == r['pinned_sweep_tests_sha256']
    for name, digest in r['protected'].items(): assert sha(ctx['protected'][name]) == digest == sha(ctx['head_protected'][name]), name
    # The control is one test, named once in the source, among the dependency controls, and the only new parent.

    assert re.search(r'test result: ok\. 1 passed; 0 failed', ctx['control_log']) and r['control_exit'] == 0
    assert re.search(r'test result: ok\. 10 passed; 0 failed', ctx['controls_log']) and r['controls_exit'] == 0
    assert ctx['live_rc'] == 0 and re.search(r'test result: ok\. 10 passed; 0 failed', ctx['live_log'])
    names = re.findall(r'^([\w:]+): test$', ctx['names'], re.M); old = re.findall(r'^([\w:]+): test$', ctx['old_names'], re.M)
    assert len(names) == len(set(names)) == r['parents'] == 207 and len(old) == r['parents_before'] == 206 and set(old) <= set(names)
    assert sorted(set(names) - set(old)) == [control] == r['parents_added']
    # The record rustc wrote: its first rule ends in a literal backslash, each outside name does, and the reader refuses it.
    f = r['fixture']; record = ctx['record']; assert record['path'] == f['record'] and record['text'] == f['text'] and record['externals'] == f['externals'] == ['a\\', 'm\\', 'z\\']
    base = f['base']; rule = 'crates/b/src/lib.rs ' + ' '.join(base + '/external/' + e for e in f['externals']); assert rule == f['rule'] and rule.endswith('\\')
    assert record['text'].startswith(record['path'] + ': ' + rule + '\n') and record['path'].startswith(base + '/' + f['output'] + '/target/chk/release/deps/b-')
    assert not record['inventory_written'] and not f['inventory_written'] and record['lib_rs'] == f['lib_rs']
    assert all('include_str!("' + base.replace('\\', '\\\\') + '/external/' + e.replace('\\', '\\\\') + '")' in f['lib_rs'] for e in f['externals'])
    scratch = base + '/' + f['output'] + '/tree/'
    assert model_reader(record['text'], record['path'], scratch, scratch) == ('ambiguous', rule, BACKSLASH)
    # The pinned Cargo refuses its own record as an internal error before the inventory reads anything.
    c = r['cargo']; stderr = ctx['cargo_stderr']; assert stderr == c['stderr'] and ctx['cargo_exit'] == c['exit'] == 101
    message = re.search(r'^error: could not parse/generate dep info at: (.*)$', stderr, re.M); assert message and message.group(0) == c['message']
    assert re.search(r'/release/deps/b-[0-9a-f]{16}\.d$', message.group(1)) and c['cause'] == 'malformed dep-info format, trailing \\'
    assert '\n\nCaused by:\n  ' + c['cause'] + '\n' in stderr and 'note: this is an unexpected cargo internal error' in stderr
    assert re.search(r'^note: ' + re.escape(c['version']) + '$', stderr, re.M) and re.fullmatch(r'cargo \d+\.\d+\.\d+ \([0-9a-f]+ \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\)', c['version'])
    assert c['version'].split()[1] == f['toolchain'].split('"')[1], 'the message is the pinned toolchain\'s Cargo'
    assert r['inventory_error'] == BUILD + record['path']
    # The control's text asserts exactly that error, no inventory, the rule's ending and the reader's refusal.
    body = source[source.index('fn ' + short + '()'):]; body = body[:body.index('\n    }\n') + 7]
    for needed in ['Err(error) => error', 'could not parse/generate dep info at: {}', 'trust-dependencies.json").exists()', 'ambiguous(super::dependency_files(', BACKSLASH,
                   'panic!("written where the build fails")', 'panic!("refused where the build fails']:
        assert needed in body, needed

def arms():
    labels = []
    def arm(label, mutate):
        altered = copy.deepcopy(ctx); mutate(altered)
        try: verify(altered)
        except AssertionError: labels.append(label); return
        raise SystemExit('altered receipt accepted: ' + label)
    def text_swap(key, a, b):
        def f(d): assert a in d[key]; d[key] = d[key].replace(a, b)
        return f
    def record_swap(a, b):
        def f(d): assert a in d['record']['text']; d['record']['text'] = d['record']['text'].replace(a, b); d['results']['fixture']['text'] = d['record']['text']
        return f
    arm('written-claimed', lambda d: d['results']['fixture'].__setitem__('inventory_written', True))
    arm('record-without-terminal-backslash', record_swap('external/z\\\n', 'external/z\n'))
    arm('escaped-backslash-claimed', record_swap('external/z\\\n', 'external/z\\\\\n'))
    arm('cargo-exit-zero', lambda d: d.__setitem__('cargo_exit', 0))
    arm('cargo-message-missing', text_swap('cargo_stderr', 'could not parse/generate dep info', 'parsed dep info'))
    arm('cause-missing', text_swap('cargo_stderr', 'malformed dep-info format, trailing \\', 'well-formed dep-info'))
    arm('internal-error-note-missing', text_swap('cargo_stderr', 'note: this is an unexpected cargo internal error', 'note: a refusal'))
    arm('foreign-cargo-version', text_swap('cargo_stderr', 'note: cargo 1.95.0', 'note: cargo 1.94.0'))
    arm('inventory-error-foreign', lambda d: d['results'].__setitem__('inventory_error', BUILD + '/elsewhere/b-0000000000000000.d'))
    arm('controls-failed', text_swap('controls_log', '10 passed; 0 failed', '9 passed; 1 failed'))
    arm('live-controls-failed', lambda d: d.__setitem__('live_rc', 101))
    arm('control-alone-failed', text_swap('control_log', '1 passed; 0 failed', '0 passed; 1 failed'))
    arm('parent-dropped', text_swap('names', 'trust::tests::every_absolute_dependency_outside_the_written_tree_is_refused: test\n', ''))
    arm('parent-foreign', text_swap('names', ctx['results']['control'] + ': test\n', ctx['results']['control'] + ': test\ntrust::tests::foreign_parent: test\n'))
    arm('control-renamed', lambda d: d['results'].__setitem__('control', 'trust::tests::another_control'))
~~~

#### The audit's first refusal

The audit's first run refused `L843.stmt.239`, the edit that stops recording a file the record names: it was killed by `54` parents, none of them in the control list as first written. The list had omitted `trust::tests::dep_info_suffix_does_not_match_an_incremental_output_path`, a dependency-record control, and `trust::tests::a_new_reader_of_a_shared_package_s_file_changes_its_readers`, which holds that a file a record names is recorded as its unit's reader; both finish the kill. Both were added; no outcome, test, source or reason changed.

#### Restoration and continuity

All `1172` regular inputs of the main tree restore against the manifest captured before the run, by `scripts/trust_adequacy.py --check-inputs`, and the plain copy restores against the same manifest with the maintained `regular_input` reader; the one Gitlink stays opaque pin metadata. The parent list is the same in the main tree and in the copy, the repair's population and the terminal-backslash control. The source, the catalogue, the reasons, the sweep and the adequacy script keep their digests. The audit refuses `10` altered receipts: a survivor claimed, a candidate dropped, a foreign finishing parent, a kill outside the block's controls, a refused edit without its error, a timeout, a historical survivor mapped elsewhere, a repair outcome changed, a parent dropped and a failing baseline.

The neighbouring consumer the repair record routed here, the catalog builder's own dependency reader in `xtask/src/catalog_build.rs`, is owned by `M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.2.1` and measured separately; `M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.2` closes with it.

```python
"""M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.2.0: select the complete current dependency block and map its history.

The block is structural: `enum Prerequisites` through `normalise_dependency_environment` (lines 393-488)
and the unit reader from opening the `.d` record to the end of its prerequisite loop (lines 794-847).
Every current candidate overlapping either range is selected from the sweep's own discovery, which is
verified against its CLI listing. The four historical survivors and the repair's 37 edits are mapped
to current IDs by exact operator, original and replacement, normalising only the guard's line-numbered
helper names and, for the historical loop, the iterator expression the repair renamed to `raws`.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, importlib.util, json, re, subprocess

out = Path('target/dependency-block-checkpoint')
file = 'xtask/src/trust.rs'
BLOCKS = [[392, 488], [793, 847]]  # zero-based half-open line ranges: lines 393-488 and 794-847


def sha(raw):
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()


spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('adequacy', 'scripts/trust_adequacy.py')
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(m)
source = Path(file).read_bytes()
assert source == subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', 'HEAD:' + file]), 'the source must be the committed one'
(out / 'source-before.rs').write_bytes(source)
lines = source.decode().split('\n')
assert lines[392].startswith('enum Prerequisites {') and lines[487] == '}'
assert lines[479].startswith('fn normalise_dependency_environment(')
assert lines[793].strip().startswith('let d = PathBuf::from(&out_dir)')
assert lines[825].strip() == 'for raw in raws {' and lines[847].strip() == 'let configuration = normalise(&tokens, &scratch);'
raw, listing, scope = m.discover(Path('scripts/mutation_sweep.sh').read_text(), source.decode())
actual = subprocess.check_output(['bash', 'scripts/mutation_sweep.sh', file, '--package', 'xtask', '--list'], text=True)
m.verify_listing(actual, listing, file, scope)
(out / 'listing.log').write_text(actual)
selected = [c for c in raw if any(m.overlaps(block, c['span']) for block in BLOCKS)]


def key(c, loop_expression=None):
    text = lambda s: re.sub(r'__archogen_sweep_\d+_', '__archogen_sweep_N_', s)
    original, replacement = text(c['original']), text(c['replacement'])
    if loop_expression:
        original = original.replace(loop_expression, 'raws')
        replacement = replacement.replace('(' + loop_expression + ')', '(raws)')
    return (c['operator'], original.strip(), replacement.strip())


current = {}
for c in selected:
    current.setdefault(key(c), []).append(c['id'])
historical_plan = json.loads(Path('target/dependency-absolute-assessment/plan.json').read_text())
history = []
loop = 'dependency_files(&text, &d, &scratch, &canonical_scratch)?'
for old, cand in zip(['L860.guard.308', 'L860.guard.309', 'L860.guard.310', 'L866.cond.312'],
                     historical_plan['candidates']):
    ids = current.get(key(cand, loop), [])
    # Each historical edit has its own text, so each maps to exactly one current candidate.
    assert len(ids) == 1, (old, ids)
    history.append({'historical': old, 'pre_repair': cand['id'], 'current': ids[0]})
assert len({h['current'] for h in history}) == 4
repair = json.loads(Path('target/dependency-path-domain-repair/plan.json').read_text())
repair_ids = [c['id'] for c in repair['candidates']]
selected_ids = [c['id'] for c in selected]
assert set(repair_ids) <= set(selected_ids), sorted(set(repair_ids) - set(selected_ids))
by_id = {c['id']: c for c in selected}
for c in repair['candidates']:
    assert key(c) == key(by_id[c['id']]), c['id']
production = source.split(b'#[cfg(test)]', 1)[0]
plan = dict(
    schema='archogen-dependency-block-checkpoint/1', status='planning-only',
    scope='The complete current dependency block of xtask/src/trust.rs (lines 393-488 and 794-847), every '
          'discovered candidate overlapping it, against the full current parent population with strict timeouts.',
    file=file, base_commit=subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip(),
    source_sha256=sha(source), production_sha256=sha(production), production_range=scope, listed_count=len(raw),
    blocks=BLOCKS, candidates=selected, equivalents=[], historical_mapping=history,
    repair_candidates=repair_ids, neighbouring_candidates=[i for i in selected_ids if i not in repair_ids],
    equivalents_sha256=sha(Path('xtask/trust.equivalents').read_bytes()),
    catalogue_sha256=sha(Path('xtask/mutations.txt').read_bytes()))
(out / 'plan.json').write_text(json.dumps(plan, indent=2) + '\n')
ops = {}
for c in selected:
    ops[c['operator']] = ops.get(c['operator'], 0) + 1
print('discovery', len(raw), 'scope', scope, 'selected', len(selected), 'repair', len(repair_ids),
      'neighbouring', len(plan['neighbouring_candidates']), ops)
for h in history:
    print(' history', h['historical'], '->', h['pre_repair'], '->', h['current'])
```

<summary>Supplemental adapter: run-native.py</summary>

```python
"""M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.2.0: run the complete dependency block against the full parent population.

Runs the sweep's own command for every selected candidate under the write-fenced profile, audits the
native log exactly with the maintained auditor, records every outcome whatever it is, and then proves the
original and copied inputs restored and the copied parent list unchanged. Judgment is the audit's.
"""
from pathlib import Path
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import hashlib, importlib.util, json, os, re, subprocess, time

root = Path.cwd()
out = Path('target/dependency-block-checkpoint')
file = 'xtask/src/trust.rs'
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('adequacy', 'scripts/trust_adequacy.py')
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(m)


def sha(raw):
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()


plan = json.loads((out / 'plan.json').read_text())
assert plan['source_sha256'] == sha(Path(file).read_bytes())
names = re.findall(r'^([\w:]+): test$', (out / 'parent-list.log').read_text(), re.M)
assert len(names) == len(set(names)) == 207, len(names)
protected = {name: sha(Path(name).read_bytes()) for name in
             [file, 'xtask/mutations.txt', 'xtask/trust.equivalents', 'scripts/mutation_sweep.sh', 'scripts/trust_adequacy.py']}
command = ['bash', 'scripts/mutation_sweep.sh', file, '--package', 'xtask', '--timeout', '600',
           '--filter=trust::', '--filter=trust_generated::', '--filter=trust_gate::', '--filter=--skip',
           '--filter=route_tests', '--timeouts-fail', '--equivalents', 'xtask/trust.equivalents']
for candidate in plan['candidates']:
    command += ['--only', candidate['id']]
profile = out / 'mutation-volume.sb'
execution = dict(command=command, base_commit=plan['base_commit'], source_sha256=plan['source_sha256'],
                 plan_sha256=sha((out / 'plan.json').read_bytes()),
                 input_manifest_sha256=sha((out / 'inputs-before.json').read_bytes()), profile=str(profile),
                 profile_sha256=sha(profile.read_bytes()), writable_root='.', protected=protected,
                 semantic_parents=len(names), started=time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z'),
                 scope='The complete current dependency block, 64 candidates, full current 207 parent population; '
                       'actual outcomes pending.')
(out / 'execution.json').write_text(json.dumps(execution, indent=2) + '\n')
error = None
measured = None
try:
    with (out / 'native.log').open('w') as log:
        result = subprocess.run(['/usr/bin/sandbox-exec', '-D', 'WRITABLE_ROOT=' + str(root), '-f', str(profile), *command],
                                stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, env=dict(os.environ, PYTHONUNBUFFERED='1'))
    (out / 'native.exit').write_text(str(result.returncode) + '\n')
    measured = m.audit_measurement((out / 'native.log').read_text(), plan, file, result.returncode)
    (out / 'measurement.json').write_text(json.dumps(measured, indent=2) + '\n')
    assert len(measured['entries']) == len(plan['candidates'])
    for row in measured['entries']:
        if row['outcome'] == 'killed':
            assert row['names'] and set(row['names']) <= set(names), row
except Exception as caught:
    error = caught
    (out / 'measurement-refusal.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(status='refused', error=repr(caught))) + '\n')
finally:
    subprocess.run(['python3', '-I', '-B', 'scripts/trust_adequacy.py', '--check-inputs', str(out / 'inputs-before.json'),
                    '--output', str(out / 'original-restoration.json')], check=True)
    expected = json.loads((out / 'inputs-before.json').read_text())
    copy_root = root / 'target/mutation-sweep/tree'
    items = [(name, {'index_mode': row['index_mode'], 'index_oid': row['index_oid']})
             for name, row in expected['regular'].items()]
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
        actual = dict(pool.map(lambda item: m.regular_input(copy_root, item), items))
    assert actual == expected['regular']
    (out / 'copy-restoration.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(
        status='restored', qualification='Maintained regular_input; borrowed index metadata, no copied Git index or '
                                         'submodule implementation claim.', regular=actual), indent=2) + '\n')
    print(len(actual), 'current copied inputs restored', flush=True)
listing = subprocess.run(['cargo', 'test', '-q', '-p', 'xtask', '--', '--list', 'trust::', 'trust_generated::',
                          'trust_gate::', '--skip', 'route_tests'], cwd=copy_root,
                         env=dict(os.environ, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=str(root / 'target/mutation-sweep/target'),
                                  ARCHOGEN_SWEEP_SOURCE=str(root)), capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
(out / 'copied-parent-list.log').write_text(listing.stdout + listing.stderr)
assert re.findall(r'^([\w:]+): test$', listing.stdout, re.M) == names
for name, digest in protected.items():
    assert sha(Path(name).read_bytes()) == digest, name
execution['finished'] = time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z')
(out / 'execution.json').write_text(json.dumps(execution, indent=2) + '\n')
if error:
    raise error
print('Dependency-block checkpoint:', json.dumps(measured['counts']), 'raw exit', measured['raw_exit_code'],
      '; original/copied inputs, all 207 parents and', len(protected), 'protected bindings restore')
```

<summary>Supplemental adapter: audit.py</summary>

```python
"""M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.2.0: the independent audit of the complete dependency-block replay.

Re-derives the selection from the sweep's own discovery and the committed source, re-reads every
outcome from the native log through the maintained auditor, and judges: each kill finishes in at least
one of the block's own controls; each unviable edit carries its actual compiler error; no survivor,
timeout, unjudged or equivalent outcome; the four historical survivors and the repair's 37 edits mapped
by exact text; full original and copied restoration. Falsifying arms alter one receipt each.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import copy as copying, hashlib, importlib.util, json, re, subprocess, sys

out = Path('target/dependency-block-checkpoint')
file = 'xtask/src/trust.rs'
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('adequacy', 'scripts/trust_adequacy.py')
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(m)
CONTROLS = {'trust::tests::' + n for n in [
    'a_final_prerequisite_ending_in_a_backslash_is_the_builds_own_error',
    'a_trailing_backslash_before_an_in_tree_prerequisite_is_refused_as_ambiguous',
    'an_ambiguous_dependency_record_is_refused_by_its_raw_rule',
    'a_symbolic_output_root_accepts_raw_and_canonical_in_tree_inputs',
    'cargo_dependency_environment_normalizes_escaped_scratch_paths',
    'cargo_dependency_information_retains_actual_source_paths',
    'dependency_environment_uses_the_canonical_encoded_prefix',
    'dependency_information_requires_its_known_nonempty_target',
    'every_absolute_dependency_outside_the_written_tree_is_refused',
    'outside_inputs_with_spaces_are_refused_by_their_raw_rule',
    'compiled_environment_refusals_cover_nonterminal_records',
    'compiled_environment_refuses_package_namespace_lookalikes',
    'a_shared_package_s_environment_is_in_its_item_and_a_foreign_variable_is_refused',
    'a_shared_package_item_holds_every_compiled_environment_value',
    'a_separator_inside_an_environment_value_cannot_hide_a_configuration_change',
    'shared_environment_records_keep_their_boundaries',
    'temporary_process_paths_are_not_admitted_as_compiled_environment_inputs',
    # Added after the first run refused L843.stmt.239: the dependency-record control the first list omitted,
    # and the control that a file a record names is recorded as its unit's reader.
    'dep_info_suffix_does_not_match_an_incremental_output_path',
    'a_new_reader_of_a_shared_package_s_file_changes_its_readers',
]}


def sha(raw):
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()


def judge(plan, measured, log, names, historical, repair_measured):
    """Every claim this leaf publishes, from its receipts; raises on the first that does not hold."""
    ids = [c['id'] for c in plan['candidates']]
    assert len(ids) == 64 and len(set(ids)) == 64
    assert [e['id'] for e in measured['entries']] == ids, 'every selected candidate, in order'
    assert measured['complete_identities'] and measured['baseline_passed']
    assert set(measured['counts']) <= {'killed', 'unviable'}, measured['counts']
    assert measured['raw_exit_code'] == 0
    assert CONTROLS <= set(names) and len(names) == 207
    rows = []
    for e in measured['entries']:
        if e['outcome'] == 'killed':
            assert e['names'] and set(e['names']) <= set(names), e['id']
            own = sorted(set(e['names']) & CONTROLS)
            assert own, ('no finishing kill in the block\'s own controls', e['id'])
            rows.append(dict(id=e['id'], outcome='killed', controls=own, finishing=len(e['names'])))
        else:
            assert e['outcome'] == 'unviable' and not e['names'], e['id']
            error = re.search(r'error\[E\d{4}\]: [^\n]*', e['detail'])
            assert error, ('an unviable edit names its actual compiler error', e['id'])
            line = [l for l in log.splitlines() if re.match(r'\s*· ' + re.escape(e['id']) + r'\s+unviable', l)]
            assert len(line) == 1 and error.group(0) in line[0], e['id']
            rows.append(dict(id=e['id'], outcome='unviable', error=error.group(0)))
    by_id = {r['id']: r for r in rows}
    for h in historical:
        assert by_id[h['current']]['outcome'] == 'killed', h
    previous = {e['id']: e['outcome'] for e in repair_measured['entries']}
    assert set(previous) == set(plan['repair_candidates'])
    for i, outcome in previous.items():
        assert by_id[i]['outcome'] == outcome, (i, outcome, by_id[i]['outcome'])
    return rows


if __name__ == '__main__':
    plan = json.loads((out / 'plan.json').read_text())
    source = Path(file).read_bytes()
    assert sha(source) == plan['source_sha256'] and source == (out / 'source-before.rs').read_bytes()
    assert source == subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', plan['base_commit'] + ':' + file])
    raw, listing, scope = m.discover(Path('scripts/mutation_sweep.sh').read_text(), source.decode())
    assert [c for c in raw if any(m.overlaps(b, c['span']) for b in plan['blocks'])] == plan['candidates']
    m.verify_listing((out / 'listing.log').read_text(), listing, file, scope)
    log = (out / 'native.log').read_text()
    exit_code = int((out / 'native.exit').read_text())
    measured = m.audit_measurement(log, plan, file, exit_code)
    assert measured == json.loads((out / 'measurement.json').read_text())
    names = re.findall(r'^([\w:]+): test$', (out / 'parent-list.log').read_text(), re.M)
    copied = re.findall(r'^([\w:]+): test$', (out / 'copied-parent-list.log').read_text(), re.M)
    assert names == copied
    repair = json.loads(Path('target/dependency-path-domain-repair/measurement.json').read_text())
    rows = judge(plan, measured, log, names, plan['historical_mapping'], repair)
    for name in ['original-restoration.json', 'copy-restoration.json']:
        assert json.loads((out / name).read_text())['status'] in ['restored', 'passed', 'verified'], name
    execution = json.loads((out / 'execution.json').read_text())
    for name, digest in execution['protected'].items():
        assert sha(Path(name).read_bytes()) == digest, name
    assert execution['plan_sha256'] == sha((out / 'plan.json').read_bytes())
    inputs = json.loads((out / 'inputs-before.json').read_text())
    # Falsifying arms: each alters one receipt and must be refused.
    arms = []

    def arm(label, alter, target='measured'):
        state = dict(plan=copying.deepcopy(plan), measured=copying.deepcopy(measured), log=log, names=list(names),
                     historical=copying.deepcopy(plan['historical_mapping']), repair=copying.deepcopy(repair))
        alter(state)
        try:
            judge(state['plan'], state['measured'], state['log'], state['names'], state['historical'], state['repair'])
        except AssertionError:
            arms.append(label)
            return
        raise SystemExit('falsifying arm accepted: ' + label)

    first_kill = next(i for i, e in enumerate(measured['entries']) if e['outcome'] == 'killed')
    first_unviable = next(i for i, e in enumerate(measured['entries']) if e['outcome'] == 'unviable')
    arm('a survivor claimed', lambda s: s['measured']['entries'][first_kill].update(outcome='survived', names=[]))
    arm('a dropped candidate', lambda s: s['measured']['entries'].pop())
    arm('a foreign finishing parent', lambda s: s['measured']['entries'][first_kill]['names'].append('trust::tests::no_such_test'))
    arm('a kill outside the block controls', lambda s: s['measured']['entries'][first_kill].update(
        names=[n for n in s['measured']['entries'][first_kill]['names'] if n not in CONTROLS] or ['trust::tests::x']))
    arm('an unviable edit without its error', lambda s: s['measured']['entries'][first_unviable].update(detail=' — it did not build'))
    arm('a strict exit claimed passing on a timeout', lambda s: s['measured']['counts'].update(timeout=1))
    arm('a historical survivor mapped elsewhere', lambda s: s['historical'][0].update(current=next(
        e['id'] for e in s['measured']['entries'] if e['outcome'] == 'unviable')))
    arm('a repair outcome changed', lambda s: s['repair']['entries'][0].update(outcome='unviable'))
    arm('a parent dropped from the population', lambda s: s['names'].pop())
    arm('the baseline failing', lambda s: s['measured'].update(baseline_passed=False))
    counts = {k: sum(r['outcome'] == k for r in rows) for k in ['killed', 'unviable']}
    result = dict(status='passed', selected=len(rows), counts=counts, raw_exit_code=measured['raw_exit_code'],
                  parents=len(names), historical={h['historical']: h['current'] for h in plan['historical_mapping']},
                  repair_edits=len(plan['repair_candidates']), neighbouring_edits=len(plan['neighbouring_candidates']),
                  restored_inputs=len(inputs['regular']), falsifying_arms_refused=len(arms), rows=rows,
                  operator_counts=measured['operator_counts'])
    (out / 'audit.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')
    print('Dependency-block audit passed:', json.dumps(counts), 'of', len(rows), 'against', len(names), 'parents; raw exit',
          measured['raw_exit_code'], ';', len(arms), 'of', len(arms), 'falsifying arms refused; sha256',
          sha((out / 'audit.json').read_bytes()))
```

```python
"""M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.2.0: the annex record of the complete dependency-block checkpoint.

Appends one section to `docs/book/src/annex-trust-proofs.md`, every figure read from the audited receipts
and every receipt or adapter a reader needs embedded whole. Keeps the annex as it was in `book-before.md`.
Figures sit in code spans: they are receipts quoted, gated by the audit that wrote them.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import json

out = Path('target/dependency-block-checkpoint')
B = chr(96)


def q(s):
    return B + str(s) + B


def fence(text, language):
    ticks = B * 3 if B * 3 not in text else '~~~'
    return ticks + language + '\n' + text + ('' if text.endswith('\n') else '\n') + ticks + '\n'


def details(title, body):
    return '\n<details>\n<summary>' + title + '</summary>\n\n' + body + '\n</details>\n'


audit = json.loads((out / 'audit.json').read_text())
plan = json.loads((out / 'plan.json').read_text())
refusal = json.loads((out / 'first-audit-refusal.json').read_text())
inputs = json.loads((out / 'inputs-before.json').read_text())
assert audit['status'] == 'passed'
rows = {r['id']: r for r in audit['rows']}
counts = audit['counts']
p = Path('docs/book/src/annex-trust-proofs.md')
base = p.read_text()
(out / 'book-before.md').write_text(base)

f = '\n\n### Complete dependency-block checkpoint\n\n'
f += ('The complete current dependency block of ' + q('xtask/src/trust.rs') + ' was replayed on ' + q('2026-10-21')
      + ' (' + q('M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.2.0') + '): ' + q(audit['selected']) + ' edits against all ' + q(audit['parents'])
      + ' current parents with strict timeouts under the write-fenced sweep, **' + q(counts['killed']) + ' killed and '
      + q(counts['unviable']) + ' refused by the compiler, raw strict exit ' + q(audit['raw_exit_code']) + '**. Every '
      'kill finishes in at least one of the block\'s own controls; every refused edit carries the compiler\'s actual '
      'error. There is no survivor, timeout, unjudged or equivalent outcome, and no reason was added or used. The four '
      'historical survivors of the initial assessment are killed. This is a measurement: production, tests, reasons '
      'and the catalogue are unchanged, and broader adequacy — the compiler, caller and global sweeps and the '
      'independent review — stays open.\n\n')
f += '#### The block, defined by structure\n\n'
f += ('The block is not the lines a repair changed. It is the reader and what it hands back — ' + q('enum Prerequisites')
      + ', ' + q('dependency_files') + ' and ' + q('normalise_dependency_environment') + ', lines ' + q('393') + ' to '
      + q('488') + ' — and the unit reader from opening the ' + q('.d') + ' record to the end of its prerequisite '
      'loop, lines ' + q('794') + ' to ' + q('847') + ': the environment records, the reader\'s two outcomes, the '
      'scratch prefixes stripped, the absolute path refused and the lexical climb refused. Every candidate the sweep\'s '
      'own discovery lists overlapping either range is selected, its listing verified against the sweep\'s CLI: '
      + q(audit['selected']) + ' of the ' + q(plan['listed_count']) + ' discovered — the repair\'s '
      + q(audit['repair_edits']) + ' and ' + q(audit['neighbouring_edits']) + ' neighbours it did not touch, among them '
      'the empty-rule refusal, the environment-record loop and its allow-list, the absolute-path branch and the '
      'insertion of a read file. The source is the committed one, ' + q(plan['source_sha256']) + ', at '
      + q(plan['base_commit']) + '.\n\n')
f += '#### The historical survivors, mapped by text\n\n'
f += ('Each historical edit maps to exactly one current candidate by its operator, original and replacement, '
      'normalising only the guard\'s line-numbered helper names and the loop\'s iterator, which the repair renamed '
      'from the reader\'s call to ' + q('raws') + '.\n\n')
f += '| Historical ID | Before the repair | Current ID | Outcome | Block controls finishing it |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n'
for h in plan['historical_mapping']:
    r = rows[h['current']]
    f += ('| ' + q(h['historical']) + ' | ' + q(h['pre_repair']) + ' | ' + q(h['current']) + ' | ' + r['outcome']
          + ' | ' + ', '.join(q(c) for c in r['controls']) + ' |\n')
f += ('\nThe repair\'s ' + q(audit['repair_edits']) + ' edits keep exactly the outcomes its own run measured against '
      'one parent fewer.\n\n')
f += '#### Every outcome\n\n'
f += '| Current ID | Outcome | Block controls finishing it, or the compiler\'s error | Finishing parents |\n| --- | --- | --- | ---: |\n'
for c in plan['candidates']:
    r = rows[c['id']]
    if r['outcome'] == 'killed':
        f += '| ' + q(r['id']) + ' | killed | ' + ', '.join(q(x) for x in r['controls']) + ' | ' + str(r['finishing']) + ' |\n'
    else:
        f += '| ' + q(r['id']) + ' | unviable | ' + q(r['error']) + ' | — |\n'
f += '\n| Operator | Attempted | Unviable |\n| --- | ---: | ---: |\n'
for op, v in sorted(audit['operator_counts'].items()):
    f += '| ' + q(op) + ' | ' + str(v['attempted']) + ' | ' + str(v['unviable']) + ' |\n'
f += ('\nThe refused edits are the compiler\'s, not the sweep\'s: four narrow a character search on a string to a '
      'slice method a ' + q('&str') + ' lacks, one comments out the push whose element type the vector is inferred '
      'from, and one comments out the ' + q('continue') + ' that gives an ' + q('else if') + ' arm its type.\n\n')
f += '#### The audit\'s first refusal\n\n'
f += ('The audit\'s first run refused ' + q(refusal['refused']) + ', the edit that stops recording a file the record '
      'names: it was killed by ' + q('54') + ' parents, none of them in the control list as first written. The list '
      'had omitted ' + q('trust::tests::dep_info_suffix_does_not_match_an_incremental_output_path') + ', a '
      'dependency-record control, and ' + q('trust::tests::a_new_reader_of_a_shared_package_s_file_changes_its_readers')
      + ', which holds that a file a record names is recorded as its unit\'s reader; both finish the kill. Both were '
      'added; no outcome, test, source or reason changed.\n\n')
f += '#### Restoration and continuity\n\n'
f += ('All ' + q(audit['restored_inputs']) + ' regular inputs of the main tree restore against the manifest captured '
      'before the run, by ' + q('scripts/trust_adequacy.py --check-inputs') + ', and the plain copy restores against '
      'the same manifest with the maintained ' + q('regular_input') + ' reader; the one Gitlink stays opaque pin '
      'metadata. The parent list is the same in the main tree and in the copy, the repair\'s population and the '
      'terminal-backslash control. The source, the catalogue, the reasons, the sweep and the adequacy script keep '
      'their digests. The audit refuses ' + q(audit['falsifying_arms_refused']) + ' altered receipts: a survivor '
      'claimed, a candidate dropped, a foreign finishing parent, a kill outside the block\'s controls, a refused edit '
      'without its error, a timeout, a historical survivor mapped elsewhere, a repair outcome changed, a parent '
      'dropped and a failing baseline.\n\n')
f += ('The neighbouring consumer the repair record routed here, the catalog builder\'s own dependency reader in '
      + q('xtask/src/catalog_build.rs') + ', is owned by ' + q('M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.2.1') + ' and measured '
      'separately; ' + q('M3.6.9.6.3.2.2.15.2.1.6.2') + ' closes with it.\n')
f += details('The historical mapping and the selected candidates', fence(json.dumps(dict(
    historical_mapping=plan['historical_mapping'], repair_candidates=plan['repair_candidates'],
    neighbouring_candidates=plan['neighbouring_candidates'], blocks=plan['blocks']), indent=2), 'json'))
f += details('The native sweep log', fence((out / 'native.log').read_text(), 'text'))
f += details('The audit\'s first refusal', fence((out / 'first-audit-refusal.json').read_text(), 'json'))
for name in ['plan.py', 'run-native.py', 'audit.py', 'publish.py']:
    f += details('Supplemental adapter: ' + name, fence((out / name).read_text(), 'python'))
f += ('\nThe receipts are under ' + q('target/dependency-block-checkpoint/') + '. The adapters are supplemental; the '
      'maintained sweep, its auditor and the input census are primary.\n')
(out / 'book-fragment.md').write_text(f)
p.write_text(base + f)
print('published', len(f), 'bytes')
```
